prompt: We need a Terraform template that creates a versatile AWS KMS module capable of managing customer master keys, replica keys, imported external key material, aliases, and key grants for centralized encryption management. The template must support mutually exclusive creation flags to provision either a standard AWS-managed KMS key, an external KMS key with base64 key material, a standard multi-region replica key referencing a primary key ARN, or a replica external key with custom key material and primary external key ARN. Key policy generation must be dynamically constructed based on role inputs, supporting a default root policy, key owners, administrators, standard key users, service users, EC2 Auto Scaling roles, specific cryptographic operation users (symmetric, HMAC, asymmetric public encryption, asymmetric sign/verify), Route 53 DNSSEC signing service permissions, and custom policy statements or override documents. Finally, the module should provision KMS aliases using exact names or name prefixes, as well as KMS grants with grantee principals, allowed operations, retiring principals, and optional encryption context constraint subsets.

We need a Terraform template that creates an Amazon SNS topic and subscription architecture supporting server-side encryption and delivery feedback logging. The template must support optional creation of a dedicated KMS key with a 7-day key deletion window, key rotation enabled, and an automated key policy permitting CloudWatch Logs service encryption and account root administration, while automatically assigning an alias prefixed with "alias/sns/" derived from the topic name. KMS encryption for the SNS topic must dynamically select between the newly created KMS key ARN, an explicitly provided KMS master key ARN, or fallback to "alias/aws/sns" depending on input configurations. Additionally, the setup must support optional creation of an SNS topic policy using a custom JSON string, feedback role ARNs and sample rates for Application, HTTP, Lambda, SQS, and Firehose endpoints, FIFO topic settings with content-based deduplication, and a dynamic map of subscriptions supporting flexible endpoint, protocol, auto-confirmation, raw message delivery, filter policy, and redrive policy parameters.

We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive IAM access management infrastructure to organize development team permissions and EC2 instance access. The configuration must feature independent boolean creation toggles for an IAM developer group, an IAM read-only and S3 full access policy, the group policy attachment, IAM users, an EC2 console screenshot policy, the user policy attachments, group membership associations, and an EC2 instance role. Default settings must configure an IAM group named "developers", a list of default users including "jack" and "jones" tagged with "user_created_by" set to "terraform", an IAM policy named "iam_read_only_and_s3_full_access" containing default statements for IAM read actions and S3 full access attached to the group, an IAM policy named "ec2_get_console_screenshot" granting EC2 console screenshot permissions attached directly to each created user, user membership in the developers group, and an EC2 assume role named "instance_role" attached to the AWS-managed "IAMReadOnlyAccess" policy ARN.

We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive AWS Backup solution to centralize data protection, automated backup schedules, and vault notifications across enterprise workloads. The template must feature independent boolean toggles to conditionally create a backup vault, a backup plan, resource backup selections, global settings, region settings, vault access policies, and vault event notifications. Default naming conventions should construct resource names using a prefix variable defaulting to "TEST" and an environment variable defaulting to "STAGE" transformed to lowercase (such as "test-backup-vault-stage", "test-backup-plan-stage", and "test-backup-selection-stage") unless explicit names are provided. Global settings should default cross-account backup preferences to enabled, while region settings must provide opt-in service preferences defaulting to DynamoDB, Aurora, EBS, EC2, EFS, FSx, RDS, and Storage Gateway. The backup plan should support complex dynamic rules featuring target vault association, cron schedules, start and completion windows, recovery point tags, cold storage and deletion lifecycle transitions, and cross-region or cross-vault copy actions with nested lifecycles. Resource selections must support IAM role authentication, explicit resource ARNs, and tag-based conditions, while vault notifications must default to alerting on "BACKUP_JOB_STARTED" and "RESTORE_JOB_COMPLETED" events sent to a specified SNS topic.

We need a Terraform template that creates an n-tier network architecture with customized route table associations for infrastructure testing. The template must provision a VPC tagged as "ntier primary" with a configurable CIDR block defaulting to "10.10.0.0/16", along with seven subnets created dynamically using cidrsubnet calculated with 8 newbits across indices 0 through 6, tagged individually using a configurable name list defaulting to ["web", "app", "db", "mgmt", "web2", "app2", "db2"]. An Internet Gateway tagged as "ntier primary" must be attached to the VPC with an explicit dependency on the subnets, alongside two route tables named according to a route table list variable defaulting to ["public", "private"], where both route tables include a default route targeting "0.0.0.0/0" via the Internet Gateway. Finally, route table associations must map subnets to these route tables based on an associations map variable defaulting to public indices [0, 3, 4] associated with the public route table and private indices [1, 2, 5, 6] associated with the private route table.

We need a Terraform template that creates a multi-cluster Kubernetes networking foundation to support cross-cluster communication testing across three availability zones. The stack must deploy a VPC using the official AWS VPC module with a CIDR block of "10.0.0.0/16", configured with a single NAT gateway to service three private subnets calculated using a prefix length extension of 4 (e.g., /20 subnets at netnums 0, 1, 2) and three public subnets calculated using a prefix length extension of 8 starting at offset 48 (e.g., /24 subnets at netnums 48, 49, 50). The public subnets must be tagged with "kubernetes.io/role/elb" set to 1, the private subnets tagged with "kubernetes.io/role/internal-elb" set to 1, and all resources tagged with Blueprint matching the VPC name and GithubRepo set to "github.com/aws-ia/terraform-aws-eks-blueprints". Additionally, provision two dedicated security groups within the VPC—named "cluster1_additional_sg" and "cluster2_additional_sg"—where each security group includes explicit egress rules permitting all protocols to "0.0.0.0/0" and "::/0", alongside reciprocal ingress rules allowing unrestricted cross-security-group communication between cluster1 and cluster2 across all protocols.

We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive, highly configurable AWS Cognito User Pool stack to manage user authentication, client app integration, and custom domain routing. The template must declare default variables for the pool name ("Pool name"), alias attributes (["email", "phone_number"]), auto-verified attributes (defaulting to empty), email verification message ("Some message {####}"), email verification subject ("Some subject"), MFA configuration ("OPTIONAL"), SMS authentication message ("SMS authentication message {####}"), SMS verification message ("SMS verification message {####}"), verification message template by link, SMS configuration map (with empty external ID and SNS caller ARN), recovery mechanisms (verified_email with priority 2, verified_phone_number with priority 1), invite message templates, admin create user only flag (defaulting to false), software token MFA enabling (defaulting to true), case sensitivity option (defaulting to null), dynamic device configuration parameters (defaulting to null), optional Lambda trigger configuration map (defaulting to empty), and custom schema definitions (defaulting to a required, mutable string email attribute). The module must conditionally provision SMS configuration when both external ID and SNS caller ARN are non-empty, software token MFA, username case sensitivity, device configuration, custom email sender Lambda triggers, and handle schema definitions with or without min/max string constraints while ignoring changes to estimated_number_of_users. Additionally, support dynamic iteration over a list of client app names defaulting to empty, creating User Pool Clients configured with generate_secret defaulting to false, token validities (access token: 120, ID token: 120, refresh token: 7) paired with token_validity_units (access_token: "minutes", id_token: "minutes", refresh_token: "days"), allowed OAuth user pool client flag (defaulting to false), token revocation (defaulting to true), explicit auth flows (["ALLOW_REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH", "ALLOW_USER_PASSWORD_AUTH", "ALLOW_USER_SRP_AUTH"]), prevent_user_existence_errors ("LEGACY"), and configurable read/write attributes, callback URLs, logout URLs, OAuth flows, OAuth scopes, and supported identity providers. Furthermore, conditionally create a Cognito user group when a group name variable is non-empty (accepting precedence defaulting to 0 and an optional IAM role ARN), a Cognito User Pool domain when a domain string variable is non-empty (accepting an optional ACM certificate ARN), and an alias Route 53 A-record targeting the domain CloudFront distribution ARN (using fixed CloudFront zone ID "Z2FDTNDATAQYW2") when a create_route53_record boolean flag defaulting to false is set to true alongside a provided Route 53 zone ID.

We need a Terraform template that creates a custom three-subnet VPC network layout with public and private routing capabilities to support general application deployment testing. The configuration must declare variables for a VPC CIDR block defaulting to "10.0.0.0/16", VPC name defaulting to "DevOps-Project-VPC", Internet Gateway name defaulting to "devops-project-igw", route table name defaulting to "DevOps-project-RT", public subnet identifier name defaulting to "subnet_a", NAT gateway name defaulting to "DevOps-NAT-GW", and a BYOIP pool name defaulting to "amazon". It must define three subnets with configurable CIDR blocks, availability zones, public IP mapping flags, and name tags, defaulting as follows: Subnet A with CIDR "10.0.1.0/24", the first availability zone in the region, public IP mapping true, and name "Subnet-A-Public"; Subnet B with CIDR "10.0.2.0/24", the second availability zone in the region, public IP mapping false, and name "Subnet-B-Private"; and Subnet C with CIDR "10.0.3.0/24", a third, distinct availability zone in the region, public IP mapping false, and name "Subnet-C-Private". The VPC must enable DNS support and hostnames, attach the tagged Internet Gateway, and include a route table tagged with the route table name that contains a default route targeting "0.0.0.0/0" via the Internet Gateway, associated explicitly only with Subnet A. Additionally, provision a VPC-scoped Elastic IP using the configured BYOIP IPv4 pool to deploy a NAT gateway tagged with the NAT gateway name inside Subnet B with an explicit dependency on the Internet Gateway, alongside a custom security group named "DefaultSecurityGroup" within the VPC that permits all outbound egress traffic.

We need a Terraform template that creates a complete AWS Backup solution with automated multi-tiered backup plans, resource selection rules, IAM permissions, and optional notification configurations for enterprise backup management. The infrastructure must provision a KMS key with key rotation enabled to encrypt an AWS Backup vault whose name defaults to "my-backup-vault", accepting optional resource tags. It must set up an IAM role assumed by backup.amazonaws.com attached to the managed AWSBackupServiceRolePolicyForBackup policy to execute backup operations. The template must construct three distinct backup plans named after the vault with suffixes "-daily", "-weekly", and "-monthly"—each containing an advanced backup setting enabling WindowsVSS for EC2 resources, along with corresponding backup selections named "daily_backup_selection", "weekly_backup_selection", and "monthly_backup_selection" targeting all resources ("*") matching string-like tag conditions on a configurable tag key defaulting to "backup" for values "daily", "weekly", and "monthly", respectively. The daily backup plan rule ("daily_backup_rule") must use a default schedule of "cron(0 12 ? * * *)", a lifecycle deletion threshold of 7 days, and an optional continuous backup flag defaulting to false; the weekly backup plan rule ("weekly_backup_rule") must use a default schedule of "cron(0 12 ? * 1 *)" and a lifecycle deletion threshold of 31 days; and the monthly backup plan rule ("monthly_backup_rule") must use a default schedule of "cron(0 12 1 * ? *)" and a lifecycle deletion threshold of 366 days. Finally, the template must conditionally provision backup vault notifications controlled by a boolean flag defaulting to false, sending alerts to a specified SNS topic ARN for a configurable event list defaulting to BACKUP_JOB_FAILED, RESTORE_JOB_FAILED, COPY_JOB_FAILED, S3_BACKUP_OBJECT_FAILED, and S3_RESTORE_OBJECT_FAILED.

We need a Terraform template that creates a multi-AZ highly available VPC network architecture with redundant NAT gateways for testing environment deployments. The template must configure input variables for an AWS region defaulting to "us-east-1", an environment tag ("env") defaulting to "test", a VPC CIDR defaulting to "10.0.0.0/16", public subnet CIDRs defaulting to ["10.0.10.0/24", "10.0.11.0/24"], private subnet CIDRs defaulting to ["10.0.20.0/24", "10.0.21.0/24"], and common tags containing an Owner of "Valerii Vasianovych" and Project of "Terraform AWS". The VPC must be named using the environment tag value followed by "-vpc", carry a custom tag recording the current AWS region merged with the common tags, and attach an Internet Gateway named using the environment tag value followed by "-igw". Public subnets must map public IPs on launch, be spread across the available availability zones in the region, be named using the environment tag value followed by "-public-subnet-" and a sequential index, and route default internet traffic ("0.0.0.0/0") through a single shared public route table named using the environment tag value followed by "-route-public-subnets". Additionally, the template must provision dedicated Elastic IPs and NAT Gateways matching the count of private subnets, placed inside the corresponding public subnets and named using the environment tag value followed by "-nat-eip-" and "-nat-gw-" plus a sequential index, paired with separate private route tables named using the environment tag value followed by "-route-private-subnets-" plus a sequential index that route outbound traffic to their respective NAT Gateway, for private subnets named using the environment tag value followed by "-private-subnet-" plus a sequential index.

We need a Terraform template that creates a conditionally deployed Amazon EKS cluster along with its required IAM service role to host containerized workloads. The infrastructure must set up an IAM role named "eks-cluster" assumed by the "eks.amazonaws.com" service principal, attached to both the managed AmazonEKSClusterPolicy and AmazonEKSVPCResourceController policies. The EKS cluster resource itself must be conditionally created based on a boolean variable named create_eks defaulting to false, configured with configurable variables for cluster_name defaulting to an empty string, cluster_version defaulting to null, and authentication_mode defaulting to "API_AND_CONFIG_MAP" while explicitly setting bootstrap_cluster_creator_admin_permissions to true. For network placement, the cluster VPC configuration must dynamically evaluate subnet options by selecting control_plane_subnet_ids if populated, otherwise falling back to subnet_ids, with both list variables defaulting to empty. Finally, enforce explicit dependencies to ensure the cluster waits for both IAM role policy attachments before creation and releases them only after cluster destruction.

We need a Terraform template that creates environment-specific IAM service accounts and access credentials for CI/CD integration across development, testing, and production environments. The stack must deploy three IAM users named "DevUser-rwwise.dev", "TestUser-rwwise.dev", and "ProdUser-rwwise.dev", each configured under the path "/system/" and tagged with a Name of "rwwise.dev Infrastructure Setup", Repository of "https://github.com/zangrum/setup.inf.rwwise.dev", and dynamic account and user IDs fetched from the current AWS caller identity context. Every user must have an active IAM access key generated alongside a dedicated inline user policy named "dev_cicd_user_policy", "test_cicd_user_policy", and "prod_cicd_user_policy", respectively. The policy documents attached to all three users must contain identical statements granting: read-only/list access to CodeBuild, CodeCommit, CloudWatch metrics, EventBridge rules/targets, and CloudWatch logs across all resources; CodeStar Connections connection lookup permissions for "arn:aws:codestar-connections:::connection/" under statement ID "CodeStarConnectionsUserAccess"; CodeStar Notifications rule description for all resources constrained by a StringLike condition on "codestar-notifications:NotificationsForResource" matching "arn:aws:codebuild:" under statement ID "CodeStarNotificationsPowerUserAccess"; and general listing access for CodeStar Notification rules, event types, and targets under statement ID "CodeStarNotificationsListAccess".

We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive, modular Amazon SNS messaging architecture including topics, standalone topic policies, endpoint subscriptions, SMS account preferences, and mobile platform applications. Global prefix variables for name ("TEST") and environment ("STAGE") must construct default lowercased resource names or display names when explicit values are not provided, and resource creation across components must be controlled by individual boolean flags defaulting to false: enable_sns_topic, enable_sns_topic_policy, enable_sns_topic_subscription, enable_sns_sms_preferences, and enable_sns_platform_application. The SNS topic component must accept mutually exclusive name or name_prefix settings, custom display names (defaulting to "lower(var.name)-sns-{lower(var.environment)}"), inline delivery or access policies, KMS encryption key IDs, and configurable success/failure feedback IAM roles and sample rates for application, HTTP, Lambda, and SQS protocols, while applying a create_before_destroy lifecycle policy. The standalone topic policy component must require a JSON policy document and automatically fall back to referencing the created SNS topic ARN if an explicit topic ARN is not provided. The subscription component must iterate over a list of endpoint strings, defaulting the protocol to "sqs", confirmation timeout to 1 minute, endpoint auto-confirms to false, raw message delivery to false, filter/delivery policies to empty strings, and falling back to the created topic ARN when an explicit topic ARN override is omitted. The SMS preferences component must support monthly spend limits, delivery status IAM roles, success sampling rates, default sender IDs, default SMS types (Promotional or Transactional), and S3 bucket usage reporting. The platform application component requires a platform type and credential string, defaults its name to "lower(var.name)-sns-plat-app-{lower(var.environment)}", and supports event notifications for delivery failure, endpoint creation, deletion, or updates alongside success/failure feedback roles and sampling rates.

We need a Terraform template that creates a customizable Amazon EventBridge event processing module to route system events to target services. The module must accept dynamic inputs for an optional name variable defaulting to null (which uses a default naming module to fall back to "default" if null or empty), a tags map defaulting to empty, a bus configuration map defaulting to empty (which validates non-null input and supports an optional event_source_name parameter defaulting to null), a rules list defaulting to empty (which validates non-null input), and a targets list defaulting to empty (which validates non-null input). A custom EventBridge bus named after the module name must be conditionally created only when the name does not equal "default". EventBridge rules defined in the rules list must be generated using each rule's name key, inheriting optional parameters for description, event_pattern, and schedule_expression (defaulting to null), while attaching to the custom event bus if created. Additionally, provision an IAM role named "-invoke" assumed by the EventBridge service principal ("events.<dns_suffix>") with an inline policy named "-invoke-targets" permitting "lambda:InvokeFunction" and "states:StartExecution" across all resources. Finally, event targets defined in the targets list must be generated with explicit dependencies on the rules, linking each target's specified rule and ARN, attaching to the custom event bus if created, and dynamically assigning the created IAM role ARN only if the target ARN contains "stateMachine".

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained AWS Backup module with dynamic resource naming, customizable lifecycle rules, and IAM service permissions for automated backup orchestration. The module must provision an IAM role prefixed with "aws-backup-" assumed by the "backup.amazonaws.com" service principal attached to the managed AWSBackupServiceRolePolicyForBackup policy. The backup vault must be named using the prefix "vault-" followed by a name value and the suffix "-backup", accept an optional KMS key ARN, tag resources with a Job tag built from the name value followed by "-backup", and conditionally attach an access policy document when a vault policy variable is non-empty. The backup plan must be named using the prefix "plan-" followed by the name value and the suffix "-backup", tagged with the same Job tag pattern, and contain a rule named using the prefix "rule-" followed by the name value and the suffix "-backup" targeting the vault, with configurable schedule parameters (start window defaulting to 60 minutes, completion window defaulting to 120 minutes), recovery point tags using the same Job tag pattern, lifecycle transitions (cold storage after 30 days, deletion after 120 days), and dynamic copy actions mapped from a destination vault map variable defaulting to empty. The backup selection must be named using the prefix "selection-" followed by the name value and the suffix "-backup", linked to the created IAM role and plan, containing an empty condition block, and filtering resources via tag selection with operation type defaulting to "STRINGEQUALS", key defaulting to "Backup", and value defaulting to "true". Finally, the vault must conditionally configure event notifications when an SNS topic ARN variable is non-empty, defaulting subscribed events to "BACKUP_JOB_FAILED" and "COPY_JOB_FAILED".

We need a Terraform template that creates a modular, enterprise-grade Amazon EFS shared storage stack to support distributed container applications. Global prefix variables for name ("TEST") and environment ("STAGE") must construct default lowercased resource names when explicit names are omitted, and resource creation across components must be governed by individual boolean flags defaulting to false: enable_efs_file_system, enable_efs_mount_target, enable_efs_file_system_policy, and enable_efs_access_point. The EFS file system component must support configurable performance modes (defaulting to "generalPurpose"), encryption flags (defaulting to true), KMS key IDs, creation tokens, provisioned throughput levels, throughput modes, and dynamic lifecycle policy rules for transition to Infrequent Access storage while enforcing a create_before_destroy lifecycle policy. The mount target component must iterate across a list of subnet IDs defaulting to empty, supporting optional specific IP addresses and security groups, falling back to the created file system ID if an explicit file system ID is omitted. The file system policy component requires a JSON policy document, falling back to the created file system ID when an explicit ID is omitted. The access point component must support POSIX user permissions (UID, GID, secondary GIDs) and root directory configurations (path, creation info with owner UID/GID and permissions), automatically falling back to the created file system ID if an explicit file system ID override is not provided.

We need a Terraform template that creates a modular AWS CodeArtifact artifact management framework containing a domain, domain permissions policy, repository, and repository permissions policy for secure package management. Global prefix variables for name ("TEST") and environment ("STAGE") must construct default lowercased resource names when explicit names are omitted, and resource creation across components must be governed by individual boolean flags defaulting to false: enable_codeartifact_domain, enable_codeartifact_domain_permissions_policy, enable_codeartifact_repository, and enable_codeartifact_repository_permissions_policy. The CodeArtifact domain component must lower-case explicit domain names or fall back to "lower(var.name)-codeartifact-domain-{lower(var.environment)}", support custom KMS encryption key ARNs, merge a default Name tag with custom tags, and enforce a create_before_destroy lifecycle policy. The domain permissions policy component requires a JSON policy document, supports optional domain owner IDs and policy revisions, and automatically falls back to referencing the created domain name if an explicit domain name is not provided. The repository component lower-cases explicit repository names or falls back to "lower(var.name)-codeartifact-repository-{lower(var.environment)}", supports descriptions, domain owner IDs, upstream repository associations, external connection configurations, merges a default Name tag with custom tags, enforces create_before_destroy, and falls back to referencing the created domain name if an explicit domain name is omitted. The repository permissions policy component requires a JSON policy document, supports domain owner IDs and policy revisions, enforces create_before_destroy, and automatically falls back to referencing the created repository name and domain name when explicit overrides are omitted.

We need a Terraform template that creates a custom cross-account IAM role and policy integration to grant third-party security auditing platform access. The infrastructure must set up an IAM role whose name is configurable via a rolename variable defaulting to "WizAccess-Role", configured with an assume role policy that allows cross-account access to an AWS principal specified by a remote-arn variable defaulting to "arn:aws:iam::830522659852:role/prod-us43-AssumeRoleDelegator", constrained by a StringEquals condition on "sts:ExternalId" matching an external-id variable defaulting to "fc959d31-537c-4108-8b87-9af9e0c9b8d2". Attach the AWS-managed ViewOnlyAccess and SecurityAudit policies to the role, alongside an inline role policy named "WizCustomPolicy" that grants explicit permissions across seven distinct policy statements: read-only access across multiple services (ACM, API Gateway, Backup, CloudTrail, CodeBuild, Cognito Identity, Connect, DynamoDB, EC2, ECR, EKS, EFS, EMR, SSM, Glacier, Glue, Health, Kafka, Kendra, Kinesis Analytics/Video, KMS, Lambda, Logs, Amazon Profiles, S3, SES, VoiceID, WAFv2, Wisdom, Macie2, Identity Store, SSO Directory, CloudWatch metrics) on all resources; EBS snapshot creation and metadata retrieval actions (CopySnapshot, CreateSnapshot, GetEbsEncryptionByDefault, DescribeSnapshots) on all resources; tag creation on "arn:aws:ec2:::snapshot/"; KMS alias creation on "arn:aws:kms:::alias/wizKey" and "arn:aws:kms:::key/*"; KMS key policy actions (GetKeyPolicy, PutKeyPolicy) on all resources matching a resource tag condition of "aws:ResourceTag/wiz" equal to "auto-gen-cmk"; snapshot deletion and modification on all resources matching an EC2 resource tag condition of "ec2:ResourceTag/wiz" equal to "auto-gen-snapshot"; and an explicit Deny statement under statement ID "WizAccessS3" for "s3:GetObject" across all resources.

We need a Terraform template that creates configurable IAM roles for admin, poweruser, and readonly access levels to manage cross-account or service-based role assumption with optional MFA enforcement. The module should allow enabling or disabling each of the three roles independently, attaching specified lists of managed policy ARNs (defaulting to AdministratorAccess, PowerUserAccess, and ReadOnlyAccess respectively), and configuring custom role names, paths, permissions boundaries, max session durations, force detach policies behavior, and resource tags. Additionally, trust policies for these roles must dynamically construct assume role statements supporting specified principal ARNs and service identifiers, with conditional MFA checks enforced per role when enabled based on a maximum MFA age threshold that defaults to 86400 seconds.

We need a Terraform template that creates a flexible AWS Transit Gateway module to support central hub-and-spoke network routing and cross-account RAM sharing. The template must include a create boolean variable defaulting to true to toggle between provisioning a new Transit Gateway or looking up an existing one (via an id variable defaulting to null or filtering by a name tag defaulting to null). When creating the Transit Gateway, both default route table association and default route table propagation must be explicitly disabled, while allowing configuration of BGP ASN defaulting to 65200, auto_accept_shared_attachments, dns_support, vpn_ecmp_support, and transit_gateway_cidr_blocks (which validates that all entries are valid IPv4 or IPv6 CIDRs). Additionally, process a map of route_tables where each item conditionally creates a new Transit Gateway route table or looks up an existing one using a transit-gateway-id filter paired with a tag:Name filter, assigning route table tags from merged global tags, local_tags, and a fallback name tag equal to the table name or the main resource name. Finally, if a shared_principals map variable contains entries, provision an AWS RAM resource share that permits external principals, defaulting its share name to an explicit ram_resource_share_name variable or the main resource name, associate the Transit Gateway to the share, and attach each principal specified in the map.

We need a Terraform template that creates a tiered AWS Backup architecture to manage automated snapshot retention across Bronze, Silver, Gold, and Premium service levels. The template must provision a shared KMS key with a 10-day deletion window and key rotation enabled, alongside an IAM role named "Bronze_Backup_Role" assumed by backup.amazonaws.com attached to the AWSBackupServiceRolePolicyForBackup and AWSBackupServiceRolePolicyForRestores managed policies. Each service tier must feature a dedicated backup vault encrypted with the shared KMS key, a corresponding backup plan, and a resource assignment filtering resources where the tag key "Backup" equals the respective tier name using a STRINGEQUALS comparison. Specifically, the Bronze tier vault ("Bronze_Backup_Vault") must pair with the "Bronze_Backup" plan containing a weekly rule ("Bronze_Backup_Weekly") scheduled at "cron(0 0 ? * FRI *)" retaining backups for 10 days, assigned via "Bronze_Resource_Assignment". The Silver tier vault ("Silver_Backup_Vault") must pair with the "Silver_Backup_Plan" containing a daily rule ("Silver_Backup_Daily") scheduled at "cron(0 5 ? * * *)" retaining backups for 7 days, assigned via "Silver_Backup_resource". The Gold tier vault ("Gold_Backup_Vault") must pair with the "Gold_Backup" plan containing three rules—a daily rule ("Gold_Daily_Backup_Rule") at "cron(0 0 * * ? *)" retaining for 31 days, a monthly rule ("Gold_Monthly_Backup_Rule") at "cron(0 0 1 1/1 ? *)" retaining for 365 days, and a yearly rule ("Gold_Yearly_Backup_Rule") at "cron(0 0 31 12 ? *)" retaining for 2555 days—assigned via "Gold_Backup_Select". Finally, the Premium tier vault ("Premium") must pair with the "Premium" plan containing four rules—a 4-hour rule ("Premium_Daily_4Hour_Backup") at "cron(0 0/4 ? * * *)" retaining for 1 day, a daily rule ("Premium_Daily_Backup") at "cron(0 0 * * ? *)" retaining for 31 days, a monthly rule ("Premium_Monthly") at "cron(0 0 1 1/1 ? *)" transitioning to cold storage after 15 days and deleting after 365 days, and a yearly rule ("Premium_Yearly") at "cron(0 0 31 12 ? *)" transitioning to cold storage after 15 days and deleting after 2555 days—assigned via "Premium".

We need a Terraform template that creates a data-driven, multi-function AWS Lambda execution environment configured via YAML inputs for serverless application deployment. The architecture must dynamically ingest function definitions either from a raw YAML configuration string variable defaulting to '"config": []' or, if empty, from a YAML configuration file path variable defaulting to "Path to the pipeline configuration file", extracting function parameters including function name, handler, runtime, source file path, architectures (defaulting to ["x86_64"]), code signing config ARN (defaulting to null), description (defaulting to empty), memory size (defaulting to 128 MB), timeout (defaulting to 3 seconds), environment variables, VPC subnets and security groups, custom IAM policy documents, CloudWatch log group names (defaulting to "/aws/lambda/"), and log retention periods (defaulting to 7 days). For every defined function, the template must provision an IAM role assumed by lambda.amazonaws.com using a configurable role name (defaulting to the function name) and path (defaulting to "/terrabits/lambda/"), attach an inline IAM policy if a custom policy document is supplied, generate a dedicated CloudWatch log group with the specified retention period, create an IAM logging policy named "<function_name>-logging" granting log creation and write permissions on "arn:aws:logs:::*" attached to the function role, and instantiate the Lambda function using base64 source hashes with dynamic VPC configurations applied when present while enforcing explicit dependencies on both the log group and logging policy attachment. Finally, all created resources must merge shared resource tags with an overarching tag setting Terraformed to true.

We need a Terraform template that creates a cross-account IAM role integration for Prisma Cloud security monitoring and compliance enforcement. The configuration must declare variables for an AWS region, an IAM role name defaulting to "PrismaCloudReadWriteRole", and a boolean flag named read_write defaulting to false. We need a Terraform template that creates a feature-rich, production-grade Amazon SNS topic module with customizable access policies, subscriptions, protocol feedback logging, and data protection rules to handle asynchronous application messaging. We need a Terraform template that creates a feature-complete Amazon S3 bucket module supporting dynamic naming, encryption, website hosting, access control, lifecycle management, CORS, logging, replication, and object lock configurations. We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained Amazon S3 datastore storage stack with scoped IAM read-only access for application image hosting. We need a Terraform template that creates a modular AWS KMS encryption management framework featuring standard customer managed keys, key aliases, grants, external key material imports, and localized ciphertext encryption for secure data management. We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive Amazon Athena analytics module to manage workgroups, databases, named queries, and data catalogs for automated data querying. We need a Terraform template that creates a modular AWS CodeBuild Continuous Integration stack supporting build projects, source credentials, webhooks, and test report groups. We need a Terraform template that creates a multi-AZ Amazon EKS-ready VPC networking foundation to host Kubernetes cluster workloads. We need a Terraform template that creates a highly configurable Amazon S3 bucket module supporting advanced access logging, static website hosting, cross-region replication, lifecycle management, object locking, and custom bucket policy controls. We need a Terraform template that creates a multi-subnet VPC network stack distributed across two availability zones for infrastructure testing. We need a Terraform template that creates an internal Application Load Balancer setup for testing path-based routing in a self-contained network. We need a Terraform template that creates a secure, centralized audit logging infrastructure using AWS CloudTrail to record all management events across the environment for compliance monitoring. We need a Terraform template that creates a managed Amazon ECR container repository with associated IAM access policies and lifecycle management for application image storage. We need a Terraform template that creates configurable AWS IAM role profiles for Administrator, PowerUser, and ReadOnly access control across multi-account environments. Provisioning for each role must be independently toggled via boolean variables defaulting to false (create_admin_role, create_poweruser_role, and create_readonly_role), with default role names set to "admin", "poweruser", and "readonly", default paths set to "/", and default policy attachments configured for "arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AdministratorAccess", "arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/PowerUserAccess", and "arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/ReadOnlyAccess" respectively. We need a Terraform template that creates an event-driven Amazon S3 bucket notification integration module supporting Lambda functions, SQS queues, and SNS topics. Overall resource creation must be controlled by a boolean variable create defaulting to true, targeting a specified bucket name (defaulting to empty) and an optional bucket_arn variable (which falls back to constructing the ARN from the bucket name if null). The module must accept map variables for lambda_notifications, sqs_notifications, and sns_notifications, dynamically configuring S3 bucket notifications with corresponding target ARNs, event lists, and optional filter_prefix or filter_suffix parameters when create is true and at least one notification map is populated. For SQS notifications, creation of SQS queue policies must be governed by a create_sqs_policy boolean defaulting to true, granting "sqs:SendMessage" permissions to "s3.amazonaws.com" conditioned on matching the bucket ARN, resolving queue URLs either from an explicit queue_id attribute or by parsing the SQS queue ARN structure. We need a Terraform template that creates a highly dynamic VPC network infrastructure for multi-tier application deployments. Furthermore, enabling NAT or private subnet options must independently provision their respective subnet sets across the configured availability zones using offset CIDR calculations.

We need a Terraform template that creates a custom VPC environment to host data processing workloads with public and private subnet structures and SSH bastion access capabilities. The network configuration must default to a primary VPC CIDR block of "10.0.0.0/16" with DNS support and DNS hostnames enabled, paired with an Internet Gateway named "demogwInternet", a public route table named "demoPublicRouteTable" sending all outbound traffic to 0.0.0.0/0 via the gateway, and a set of public subnets automatically assigning public IPs on launch mapped across specified availability zones using default CIDRs "10.0.0.0/24" and "10.0.2.0/24". The template should also define standard configurable variables with proper default values for project ("demo"), environment ("poc"), VPC name ("demo-dataflow"), region ("us-east-1"), private subnet CIDR blocks ("10.0.1.0/24" and "10.0.3.0/24"), EC2 key pair name ("kplinuxdemo"), bastion instance type ("t3.nano"), EBS optimization toggle (false), and custom resource tagging maps.

We need a Terraform template that creates a flexible VPC networking module supporting dynamically calculated subnet tiers across a configurable number of availability zones for general network partitioning. The module must feature input variables for vpc_cidr (defaulting to "10.0.0.0/16"), number_of_availability_zones (defaulting to 2), enable_public_subnets (defaulting to false), enable_nat_subnets (defaulting to false), and enable_private_subnets (defaulting to false). Subnet CIDR allocations must be calculated dynamically based on the total number of enabled subnet types multiplied by the chosen number of availability zones, calculating logarithmic newbits to slice the VPC CIDR cleanly across the requested availability zones in the region. When public subnets are enabled, the stack must create a dedicated security group with an egress rule permitting all traffic (protocol "all", ports 0 to 65535 to "0.0.0.0/0"), an internet gateway, public subnets mapped to auto-assign public IPs on launch, and a public route table routing "0.0.0.0/0" to the internet gateway alongside a local route for the VPC CIDR associated with all public subnets. Additionally, when enabled, NAT subnets and private subnets must be provisioned across the specified availability zones using sequential CIDR offset blocks based on the availability zone multiplier index.

We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive AWS IAM user management and security baseline stack to govern role-based access control and password compliance across environments. The template must configure an account password policy with variables defaulting to allowing user password changes (true), non-hard expiry (false), maximum password age of 90 days, minimum password length of 14 characters, password reuse prevention history of 24, and required lowercase, uppercase, number, and symbol characters (all true). It must provision three IAM groups named "administrators", "developpers", and "prod_users", each paired with an attached custom IAM policy. The "developpers_policy" attached to "developpers" must allow full EC2 ("ec2:") and RDS ("rds:") actions on all resources conditioned on matching the resource tag "env" equal to "dev". The "prod_users_policy" attached to "prod_users" must allow full EC2 and RDS actions on all resources conditioned on matching the resource tag "env" equal to "preprod" or "prod". The "administrators_policy" attached to "administrators" must grant broad access on all resources using a NotAction block that excludes "iam:", "organizations:", and "account:*" conditioned on the resource tag "security" not equaling "high", while explicitly permitting "iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole", "iam:DeleteServiceLinkedRole", "iam:ListRoles", "organizations:DescribeOrganization", and "account:ListRegions" across all resources.

We need a Terraform template that creates an isolated private VPC networking infrastructure with S3 gateway endpoint access for secure internal workloads. The stack must deploy a VPC configured with a variable region defaulting to "us-east-1", a resource name prefix variable defaulting to "tfm-aws", instance tenancy defaulting to "default", enabled DNS hostnames (true), enabled DNS support (true), and a main CIDR block defaulting to "10.0.0.0/16". Provision two private subnets across the first two available availability zones in the region using CIDR blocks specified by a private_subnets list variable defaulting to ["10.0.2.0/24", "10.0.3.0/24"], paired with two dedicated private route tables and subnet route table associations. Additionally, associate an S3 VPC gateway endpoint with both private route tables, and associate a shared network ACL with the private subnets containing an inbound rule and an outbound rule configured from variable lists public_inbound_acl_rules and public_outbound_acl_rules (each defaulting to rule number 100, action "allow", all protocols "-1", ports 0 to 0, and CIDR block "0.0.0.0/0").

We need a Terraform template that creates a customizable, self-contained AWS VPC base networking module supporting dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 IPAM allocations, default adoption rule resets, and internet gateways using Cloud Posse null-label context conventions. The core VPC resource must accept a primary IPv4 CIDR block defaulting to "11.0.0.0/16" (or an optional IPAM pool association), instance tenancy defaulting to "default", enabled DNS hostnames (true), enabled DNS support (true), and autogenerated IPv6 CIDR block assignment defaulting to true (with support for optional primary IPv6 IPAM associations). The stack must allow registering additional IPv4 and IPv6 CIDR block associations from map variables (supporting IPAM pools, netmask lengths, and creation/deletion timeouts). To enforce security baselines, default resource management features must allow adoption of default VPC resources, including a default security group that strips all rules when a default_security_group_deny_all variable is set to true, alongside configurable adoption flags for default route tables (defaulting to false) and default network ACLs (defaulting to false). Finally, the template must conditionally provision a standard IPv4/IPv6 internet gateway controlled by an internet_gateway_enabled boolean defaulting to true and an IPv6 egress-only internet gateway controlled by an ipv6_egress_only_internet_gateway_enabled boolean defaulting to false.

We need a Terraform template that creates a modular AWS Lambda serverless execution stack supporting functions, layer versions, aliases, event invoke configurations, permissions, provisioned concurrency, code signing, and event source mappings. Global prefix variables for name ("TEST") and environment ("STAGE") must construct default lowercased resource names when explicit names are omitted, and provisioning across components must be governed by individual boolean flags defaulting to false: enable_lambda_function, enable_lambda_alias, enable_lambda_event_source_mapping, enable_lambda_function_event_invoke_config, enable_lambda_layer_version, enable_lambda_permission, enable_lambda_provisioned_concurrency_config, and enable_code_signing_config. The Lambda function component requires an execution role ARN, handler string, runtime defaulting to "python3.7", memory size defaulting to 128 MB, timeout defaulting to 3 seconds, reserved concurrent executions defaulting to "-1", and publish flag defaulting to false, supporting deployment zip files or S3 bucket/key sources, dead letter queues, X-Ray tracing modes, VPC subnets and security groups, environment variables, KMS encryption keys, and tags. The Lambda layer version component constructs layer names defaulting to "lower(var.name)-lambda-layer-ver-{lower(var.environment)}", supporting deployment packages from local files or S3 alongside compatible runtimes. Lambda alias creation constructs alias names defaulting to "lower(var.name)-lambda-alias-{lower(var.environment)}", targeting a default version of "$LATEST" or referencing the created function ARN, with routing configurations for additional version weights ignoring change lifecycle drifts. Additional components (event invoke configs, permissions, and provisioned concurrency) must dynamically resolve target function names and qualifiers from explicit variables, falling back to created function or alias attributes depending on enabling flags, with provisioned concurrent executions defaulting to 1 and retry attempts defaulting to 2. Finally, event source mappings require an event source ARN with batch size defaulting to 100, enabled status defaulting to true, parallelization factor defaulting to 1, maximum retry attempts defaulting to 10000, maximum record age defaulting to 604800 seconds, and bisect batch on error defaulting to false.

We need a Terraform template that creates a data-driven, multi-VPC networking module to dynamically provision VPCs, subnets, internet gateways, NAT gateways, route tables, and security groups using map variables. The configuration must accept a map of VPC objects defining cidr_block, enable_dns (defaulting to true), and enable_dns_hostnames (defaulting to false), alongside default tags specifying environment set to "Dev" and managedBy set to "Terraform". Subnets must be created from a map variable specifying vpc_name, cidr_block, and availability_zone, with resource names standardized using the prefix "sn-" followed by the subnet's map key, its availability zone, and the AWS region. The template must support optional internet gateways mapped by VPC name and Elastic IP-backed NAT gateways mapped by target subnet and VPC names. Route tables must dynamically evaluate route entries mapping traffic either to specified internet gateways (when use_igw is true, defaulting to true) or NAT gateways (when use_ngw is true, defaulting to false), alongside explicit subnet route table associations. Additionally, security groups must support standalone ingress and egress rules accepting either IPv4 CIDR blocks or cross-referenced security group names, while adopting the default security group for each VPC to permit all self ingress and all egress traffic ("0.0.0.0/0").

We need a Terraform template that creates a serverless AWS Lambda execution module to deploy function code, optional Lambda layers, alias versions, CloudWatch log groups, and EFS filesystem integrations. The module must evaluate a name variable defaulting to "lambda" when null or empty (using petname generation) and tag resources with "terraform.io" set to "managed". Lambda function provisioning must be conditionally controlled by the presence of a non-empty lambda map variable (validated as non-null), defaulting handler to "lambda_handler", runtime to "python3.8", memory to 128 MB, timeout to 3 seconds, reserved concurrent executions to -1, publish to false, and supporting local deployment package paths, S3 source configurations, environment variables, X-Ray tracing modes (defaulting to "PassThrough"), VPC subnets and security groups, and EFS mount configurations (defaulting local mount path to "/mnt"). When a non-empty layer map variable is provided (validated as non-null), the template must create a Lambda layer version defaulting compatible runtimes to ["python3.8"], skip_destroy to false, and automatically attach its ARN to the function. When function aliases are defined within the lambda map, create Lambda aliases defaulting function_version to "$LATEST". Additionally, for enabled functions, create an execution IAM role named "-lambda" attached to managed policies for AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole, AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole, AmazonElasticFileSystemClientFullAccess, AWSXrayWriteOnlyAccess, custom policy ARNs from a policy_arns list variable, and write access to an integrated CloudWatch logs module using a log group namespace defaulting to "/aws/lambda" and log retention defaulting to 7 days.

We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive, modular CloudWatch monitoring and synthetic testing solution for AWS services. The module must feature individual boolean flags defaulting to false to conditionally toggle each component: enabled_basic for a single metric alarm, enabled_dynamic for map-based dynamic metric alarms, create_metric_alarm_expression for math or anomaly-detection metric query alarms, create_composite_alarm for composite alarms appending "-comp" to the base name, create_dashboard for CloudWatch dashboards, create_log_group for a log group with an associated log stream, and create_syn_canary for an Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics canary test. Standard metric alarms must tag resources with "terraform" set to true and use default metrics targeting "CPUUtilization" under "AWS/EC2" with a comparison operator of "GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold", evaluation periods of 60, period of 120 seconds, average statistic, threshold of 40, and missing data treated as "missing". Metric query expression alarms must support dynamic metric_query blocks for expressions and metrics with threshold_metric_id configuration, while composite alarms evaluate an alarm rule expression against dependency alarms. When canary testing is enabled, the template must insert a 60-second time delay before launching the canary, configuring its schedule expression as rate(1 minute) or rate(N minutes), artifact storage under "s3://{var.syn_s3_canary_bucket_name}/canary/{var.syn_canary_name}", and success retention period defaulting to 3 days.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained IAM security framework for provisioning infrastructure deployment credentials and scoped EC2/backend permissions. The stack must deploy an IAM user with force_destroy enabled using a username variable defaulting to "my_vpn_infra_user", an IAM group defined by group_name defaulting to "my-vpn-infra-group", group membership defined by membership_name defaulting to "my-vpn-infra-manager-group", and an active IAM access key for the user. All created policies and the IAM user must apply a ProjectTag tag matching a project_tag variable defaulting to "my-vpn-tag", and all policies must be attached to the IAM group using a custom policy path variable defaulting to "/my_vpn_infra/". The template must create seven distinct IAM policies attached to the group: basic_policy granting "sts:GetCallerIdentity"; create_policy granting explicit EC2 resource creation actions ("ec2:CreateKeyPair", "ec2:CreateVpc", "ec2:CreateSubnet", "ec2:CreateInternetGateway", "ec2:CreateRoute", "ec2:CreateRouteTable", "ec2:CreateLocalGatewayRouteTableVpcAssociation", "ec2:CreateSecurityGroup", "ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupEgress", "ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress", "ec2:CreateReplaceRootVolumeTask", "ec2:CreateTags", and "ec2:AllocateAddress"); read_policy granting a comprehensive set of EC2 read actions; update_policy granting EC2 modification and association actions; delete_policy granting EC2 deletion and detachment actions; instance_policy granting EC2 lifecycle actions ("ec2:RunInstances", "ec2:StartInstances", "ec2:ResetInstanceAttribute", "ec2:ModifyInstanceAttribute", "ec2:StopInstances", "ec2:TerminateInstances", and "ec2:RebootInstances"); and terraform_backend_access granting DynamoDB state lock access ("dynamodb:DescribeTable", "dynamodb:GetItem", "dynamodb:PutItem", and "dynamodb:DeleteItem") alongside S3 backend access ("s3:ListBucket", "s3:GetObject", "s3:PutObject", and "s3:DeleteObject") on all resources.

We need a Terraform template that creates a dual-tier VPC networking stack in region "us-east-1" to host public and private web workloads. The template must accept an optional existing_vpc_id variable defaulting to an empty string, falling back to creating a new VPC with enabled DNS hostnames, an environment prefix defaulting to "DEV", and a main CIDR block defaulting to "10.0.0.0/16". Provision two public subnets across two different availability zones in the region with CIDRs "10.0.1.0/24" and "10.0.2.0/24", associated with an internet gateway via a public route table routing "0.0.0.0/0". Additionally, include a boolean flag craete_private_subnet defaulting to false; when enabled, it must create two private subnets across the same two availability zones using CIDRs "10.0.10.0/24" and "10.0.11.0/24", a private route table, and a single Elastic IP-backed NAT Gateway in the first public subnet (with Elastic IP private IP association defaulting to "10.0.0.5") routing outbound "0.0.0.0/0" traffic for the private subnets.

We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive Amazon SQS messaging module supporting standard and FIFO queues, custom queue policies, dead-letter queues, redrive policies, and SSE encryption. Primary queue creation must be controlled by a boolean variable create defaulting to true, handling name or name_prefix patterns while automatically managing the .fifo suffix for FIFO queues (fifo_queue defaulting to false). SQS managed server-side encryption (sqs_managed_sse_enabled defaulting to true) must apply automatically whenever a custom KMS master key ID is omitted. Option for attached queue policies must be governed by a create_queue_policy flag defaulting to false, merging source and override policy document strings or rendering custom policy statements where resource defaults to the queue ARN when unspecified. When dead-letter queue creation is toggled on via create_dlq (defaulting to false), the template must provision a corresponding dead-letter queue (inheriting FIFO configuration, default name suffixing "-dlq", and fallback encryption settings from the main queue), attach a redrive policy to the main queue setting maxReceiveCount to 5, and attach a redrive allow policy to the dead-letter queue restricting redrive permissions byQueue to the main queue ARN when create_dlq_redrive_allow_policy is true (defaulting to true).

We need a Terraform template that creates a multi-bucket Amazon S3 storage infrastructure with customizable IAM user access keys, EKS IAM Roles for Service Accounts (IRSA), lifecycle configurations, and CloudFront origin access identities. The module must accept a list of bucket objects (each specifying a bucket name, label, optional tags, expiration lifecycle settings, and optional role service account bindings) alongside a storage_prefix variable defaulting to "quortex", a force_destroy parameter defaulting to false, an enable_bucket_encryption flag defaulting to true (enforcing AES256 server-side encryption), and public access blocks restricting all public ACLs and policies across every created bucket. User access key provisioning must be controlled by an enable_user_access_key boolean defaulting to true; when enabled and at least one bucket is specified, it must create a single IAM user named by combining the storage prefix value with "-storage", placed at an IAM path defaulting to "/system/", an IAM access key, and per-bucket inline user policies granting "s3:ListBucket" on each bucket ARN and "s3:*Object" on all object paths. When enable_irsa is set to true (defaulting to false), for every bucket with defined role service accounts, the template must provision an IAM role named by combining the storage prefix and the bucket name with the suffix "-irsa", using a web identity assume role trust policy evaluated against the cluster's OIDC issuer (matching subject claims built from each service account's namespace and name, and audience "sts.amazonaws.com"), paired with an IAM policy and role policy attachment granting the same bucket list and object permissions. Finally, when enable_cloudfront_oia is set to true (defaulting to false), create a CloudFront Origin Access Identity for each bucket and attach a bucket policy permitting "s3:GetObject" for the OAI IAM principal.

We need a Terraform template that creates a unified AWS ECR container registry management module supporting both private and public repositories with dedicated KMS encryption, cross-account permissions, and automated IAM user credential provisioning. Global resource naming and tagging must incorporate a validated name_prefix variable defaulting to "pippi-" (restricted to letters and hyphens) and apply mandatory default tags including tf-module set to "pippi.io/aws-ecr" alongside the active Terraform workspace. When private repositories are defined, the template must provision a customer-managed KMS key with automatic key rotation enabled, assigned to a policy granting root account KMS operations, to encrypt private ECR repositories using KMS encryption alongside mandatory scan-on-push image scanning and tag mutability defaulting to "MUTABLE". For defined public ECR repositories, catalog details such as description, about text, usage text, architectures, operating systems, and logo image blobs must be configured when provided. Dedicated resource policies must be attached to every private and public repository, dynamically aggregating pull and push principals from repository-specific account IDs, role ARNs, and global push/pull account lists (always including the current AWS account ID as a principal). Finally, for any private or public repository configured with create_iam_user enabled, provision an IAM user located at path "/artifact/" named with the prefix and repository key, issue an active IAM access key, and attach a user policy granting ECR authorization token retrieval alongside repository-scoped layer upload, download, and image push/pull permissions.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained IAM infrastructure for load balancer monitoring automation in the us-east-1 region. The stack must provision three system IAM users named "loadbalancer", "loadbalancer2", and "loadbalancer3", all created under the path "/system/" and equipped with active programmatic access keys. Each user must have four individual inline user policies attached directly to them granting "ec2:Describe*" permissions across all resources; specifically, user "loadbalancer" must have inline policies named "test", "test2", "test3", and "test4", user "loadbalancer2" must have inline policies named "test2", "test22", "test23", and "test24", and user "loadbalancer3" must have inline policies named "test3", "test32", "test33", and "test34".

We need a Terraform template that creates an AWS Backup vault infrastructure supporting multi-account patterns with customizable retention locking, SNS notifications, and workload-specific backup plans. The configuration must accept a required backup name variable, an account_type variable defaulting to "workload" (validated strictly to "workload" or "backup"), an optional KMS key ARN for vault encryption, and an optional vault policy string. When a min_retention_days parameter is provided, the template must configure a vault lock with optional max_retention_days and changeable_for_days. Optional vault notifications must be controlled by a boolean flag enable_aws_backup_vault_notifications (defaulting to false) to route failure events (defaulting to "BACKUP_JOB_FAILED" and "COPY_JOB_FAILED") to a specified SNS topic ARN. When account_type is set to "workload", the template must provision an IAM role prefixed with "aws-backup-" with the AWSBackupServiceRolePolicyForBackup managed policy attached, a backup plan named by combining "plan-" with the backup name value and the suffix "-backup", with configurable rule schedule, 60-minute start window, 120-minute completion window, cold storage transition after 30 days, deletion after 120 days, recovery point tagging, and dynamic cross-region or cross-account copy actions, alongside a tag-based backup selection matching key "Backup" equal to "true" using "STRINGEQUALS" and an additional resource-based selection if explicit ARNs are supplied in selection_resources.

We need a Terraform template that creates an AWS Config compliance auditing and security monitoring stack to track configuration changes and enforce security rules across all supported resources in the account. The stack must deploy an IAM role using a name generated from a naming convention module (defaulting to "config" with petname fallback when null or empty) paired with the AWS_ConfigRole managed policy, write permissions to a force-destroy-enabled S3 snapshot storage bucket, and an inline policy permitting SNS publish operations. An AWS Config configuration recorder must capture all supported global and regional resource types and deliver snapshot records with an S3 key prefix of "awsconfig/records" to the snapshot bucket while streaming notifications to an SNS topic bearing the resource name. Additionally, the template must provision a set of eleven managed AWS Config rules evaluated every twenty-four hours or upon configuration changes: "cloudtrail-enabled" (CLOUD_TRAIL_ENABLED), "iam-pw-policy" (IAM_PASSWORD_POLICY), "ec2-vpc" (INSTANCES_IN_VPC), "root-mfa-enabled" (ROOT_ACCOUNT_MFA_ENABLED), "acm-expiration-check" (ACM_CERTIFICATE_EXPIRATION_CHECK), "ebs-inuse-check" (EC2_VOLUME_INUSE_CHECK), "ec2-imdsv2-check" (EC2_IMDSV2_CHECK), "rds-encrypted" (RDS_STORAGE_ENCRYPTED), "rds-private" (RDS_INSTANCE_PUBLIC_ACCESS_CHECK), "rds-private-snapshots" (RDS_SNAPSHOTS_PUBLIC_PROHIBITED), and "required-tags" (REQUIRED_TAGS checking for "terraform.io" and "environment" tags specifically scoped to "S3::Bucket" resources).

We need a Terraform template that creates a multi-tier AWS VPC network infrastructure across three availability zones to host web application, database, and caching workloads. The stack must deploy a main VPC with CIDR block "10.0.0.0/16" and enabled DNS hostnames and DNS support, applying standard resource tags including Name, Project ("BJIT DevOps Task"), and Author ("Ariful Islam"). Provision three public subnets auto-assigning public IPs on launch with CIDR blocks "10.0.4.0/24", "10.0.6.0/24", and "10.0.8.0/24", alongside three private subnets with CIDR blocks "10.0.10.0/24", "10.0.12.0/24", and "10.0.14.0/24" mapped sequentially across three availability zones. Public subnets must connect to an Internet Gateway via a shared public route table, while private subnets associate with three zone-specific private route tables connected to an S3 VPC gateway endpoint. Additionally, create six dedicated security groups with full outbound egress ("0.0.0.0/0"): "bjit-api-server-ALB-SG" allowing HTTP/HTTPS (ports 80-443) from "0.0.0.0/0"; "bjit-mariaDB-RDS-SG" allowing MySQL/MariaDB (port 3306) from "10.0.0.0/16"; "bjit-redis-SG" allowing Redis (port 6379) from "10.0.0.0/16"; "bjit-api-server-SG" allowing ports 8080 and 22 from "10.0.0.0/16"; "bjit-file-server-SG" allowing ports 8081 and 22 from "10.0.0.0/16"; and "bjit-public-ssh-SG" allowing SSH (port 22) from "0.0.0.0/0".

We need a Terraform template that creates a scalable VPC network infrastructure with optional private subnet tiers, NAT gateways, and private VPC endpoints for secure container workloads. The template must construct a main VPC with enabled DNS hostnames using a base_name prefix variable defaulting to "benchmark" and a vpc_cidr block defaulting to "10.0.0.0/16". Public subnets must be provisioned using a subnet_public_cidrs list variable defaulting to ["10.0.1.0/24", "10.0.2.0/24"] across available availability zones starting from the second zone index, mapped to a public route table connected to an Internet Gateway with a default route for "0.0.0.0/0". Private subnets must be conditionally created based on a subnet_private_cidrs list variable defaulting to null; when private CIDRs are provided, the template must provision private subnets across matching availability zone indices, create per-public-subnet Elastic IPs and NAT Gateways with corresponding private route table entries for "0.0.0.0/0", and associate a dedicated private gateway endpoint for S3. Furthermore, the infrastructure must include an S3 gateway endpoint for public subnets, as well as HTTPS interface VPC endpoints for ECR API and ECR Docker with private DNS enabled, bound to an ECR security group that permits ingress on port 443 from all public subnet CIDRs and conditionally permits ingress on port 443 from private subnet CIDRs when private subnets are present.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained, multi-tier AWS VPC network infrastructure across two availability zones to host secure web application and database tiers. The VPC must use a default CIDR block of "10.0.0.0/16" named "project-vpc", containing two public subnets ("pub-sub-1" with default CIDR "10.0.1.0/24" and "pub-sub-2" with default CIDR "10.0.2.0/24") and two private subnets ("pvt-sub-1" with default CIDR "10.0.3.0/24" and "pvt-sub-2" with default CIDR "10.0.4.0/24") deployed across the first two available availability zones in the region. An Internet Gateway named "T-igw" must connect two dedicated public route tables ("RT_PUBRT-1" and "RT_PUBRT-2") routing default outbound traffic ("0.0.0.0/0") for each public subnet. Provision two Elastic IPs and two NAT Gateways (both tagged "T-NAT1") in the respective public subnets; both private subnets must associate with dedicated private route tables ("RT_PVTRT-1" and "RT_PVTRT-2") that route default outbound traffic ("0.0.0.0/0") through the first NAT Gateway. Additionally, configure a public security group named "allow_tls" permitting inbound HTTP (port 80), HTTPS (port 443), and SSH (port 22) from everywhere ("0.0.0.0/0") with unrestricted egress, paired with a private security group named "pvt-seg" permitting inbound HTTP, HTTPS, SSH, and PostgreSQL (port 5432) traffic exclusively from the public security group and restricting egress exclusively to the public security group.

We need a Terraform template that creates a serverless, direct API Gateway to DynamoDB integration pattern to manage a pet inventory database without relying on Lambda functions. The stack must deploy a provisioned DynamoDB table named "Pets" with a primary hash key "id" (string) set to 5 read and 5 write capacity units, alongside a global secondary index named "PetType-index" on hash key "PetType" (string) projecting non-key attributes "PetName" and "PetPrice" with 5 read and 5 write capacity units. An IAM role assuming the "apigateway.amazonaws.com" service principal must grant permissions for "dynamodb:PutItem" and "dynamodb:Query" targeting the table and its indexes. Configure an API Gateway REST API named "APIGW DynamoDB Serverless Pattern Demo" enforcing API key security via an "x-api-key" header; it must expose a POST endpoint at "/pets" integrating directly with DynamoDB PutItem using VTL request templates mapping request payloads into "Pets" items with auto-generated requestId values and PetBoolean set to true, as well as a GET endpoint at "/pets/{PetType}" integrating directly with DynamoDB Query against "PetType-index" with URL-decoded parameter substitution and VTL response mapping. The REST API must be deployed to a stage named "v1" with method settings enabling INFO level CloudWatch logging and metrics, linked to an API Gateway account CloudWatch role, a CloudWatch log group prefixed with "/aws/APIGW/terraform", and a log resource policy permitting log delivery from the REST API source ARN. Finally, security must be enforced by provisioning an API key named "apigw-dynamodb-terraform-api-key" bound to a usage plan named "apigw-dynamodb-terraform-usage-plan" configured with a burst limit of 20, rate limit of 100, and a monthly quota limit of 1000 requests associated with stage "v1".

We need a Terraform template that creates a customizable Amazon S3 storage architecture for testing security configurations and public access policies using a configurable name variable defaulting to "sadcloud". The primary bucket must be constructed with force_destroy enabled, a prefix derived from the name variable, object ownership set to "BucketOwnerPreferred", a private ACL, and versioning enabled by default unless a boolean variable no_versioning (defaulting to false) is set to true. Server-side encryption using "AES256" must be applied to the main bucket unless a boolean variable no_default_encryption (defaulting to false) disables it, and static website hosting with index document "index.html" must be conditionally configured based on a website_enabled boolean variable (defaulting to false). Logging for the main bucket must target a separate, force-destroy-enabled logging bucket named using the name value followed by the suffix "-logging", object ownership "BucketOwnerPreferred", and canned ACL defaulting to "log-delivery-write" (as defined by a bucket_acl variable), both of which are omitted if a no_logging boolean variable (defaulting to false) is set to true. Additionally, when an allow_cleartext boolean variable (defaulting to false) is true, attach an S3 bucket policy to the main bucket that explicitly denies all s3:* actions over non-SSL transport ("aws:SecureTransport" equal to "false"). Finally, the template must support optional secondary buckets with public access block restrictions completely disabled: one for public read-only access (s3_getobject_only defaulting to false) named using the name value followed by the suffix "-getonly" and an s3:GetObject policy, and another for full public read-write access (s3_public defaulting to false) named using the name value followed by the suffix "-public" and an s3:* policy.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained IAM role and policy baseline required to initialize and operate AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (DRS) across replication, conversion, failback, and recovery instances. The stack must provision seven service roles under the "/service-role/" path: AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryAgentRole and AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryFailbackRole (both allowing drs.amazonaws.com to assume the role and set source identity, conditioned on the calling account ID and source identity prefixes "s-" and "i-", respectively), alongside AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryConversionServerRole, AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryRecoveryInstanceRole, AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryReplicationServerRole, and AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryRecoveryInstanceWithLaunchActionsRole (all assuming ec2.amazonaws.com). Attach corresponding AWS-managed policies (AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryAgentPolicy, AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryFailbackPolicy, AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryConversionServerPolicy, AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryRecoveryInstancePolicy, and AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryReplicationServerPolicy) to their respective service roles, while attaching both AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryRecoveryInstancePolicy and AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore to AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryRecoveryInstanceWithLaunchActionsRole. Finally, create a root-path initializer role named AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryInitializerRole that allows the current calling identity user ID to assume it, bound to a custom InitializePolicy permitting service initialization, instance profile creation, PassRole actions for EC2 and DRS services, service-linked role creation for AWSServiceRoleForElasticDisasterRecovery, full EC2 actions, and role policy attachments restricted to the DRS managed policies.

We need a Terraform template that creates a modular AWS Config compliance and governance architecture supporting multi-account aggregators, recorders, delivery channels, organization rules, and automated remediation triggers. Global prefix variables for name ("TEST"), region ("us-east-1"), and environment ("STAGE") must construct default lowercased resource names when explicit names are omitted, and provisioning across components must be governed by individual boolean flags defaulting to false: enable_config_aggregate_authorization, enable_config_config_rule, enable_config_configuration_aggregator, enable_config_configuration_recorder, enable_config_configuration_recorder_status, enable_config_delivery_channel, enable_config_organization_managed_rule, enable_config_organization_custom_rule, and enable_config_remediation_configuration. Aggregate authorizations require an account ID and region, while configuration aggregators support account lists, region sets, or organization aggregation sources with role ARNs. The configuration recorder requires an IAM role ARN alongside dynamic recording groups, paired with a recorder status component defaulting is_enabled to true. The delivery channel component requires an S3 bucket name alongside optional S3 key prefixes, SNS topic ARNs, and snapshot delivery properties. Managed rules require rule source blocks defaulting owner to "AWS" and source identifier to "S3_BUCKET_VERSIONING_ENABLED", alongside configurable scopes for tags, resource IDs, or resource types. When organization rules are enabled alongside enable_organizations_organization (defaulting to false), support organization managed rules (defaulting identifier to "IAM_PASSWORD_POLICY") and custom Lambda rules with notification triggers (defaulting to "ConfigurationItemChangeNotification") and account exclusions. Finally, remediation configurations must target a specified or created rule name, accepting target types, target IDs, resource types, automatic execution flags, retry attempt limits, parameters, and SSM execution rate controls.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained AWS VPC infrastructure for launching private compute instances in region "us-east-1". The network configuration must provision a VPC with a default CIDR block of "10.0.0.0/16" named "VPC_from_Terraform" with DNS support and DNS hostnames enabled, tagged "Terraform" set to "true". Three private subnets must be created using CIDR blocks ["10.0.1.0/24", "10.0.2.0/24", "10.0.3.0/24"] mapped across three availability zones. A security group named "allow_ssh_http_https" tagged "Terraform_SG_HTTP_HTTPS_SSH" must be attached to the VPC, allowing inbound SSH (port 22) restricted strictly to the VPC's CIDR block, inbound HTTP (port 80) and HTTPS (port 443) from everywhere ("0.0.0.0/0"), and unrestricted egress. Finally, deploy a default count of 3 EC2 instances of type "t2.micro" using the latest Amazon Linux 2 AMI by default, distributed across the private subnets with the security group attached, named "Terraform_Instance", and configured with a 20 GB root volume tagged "Terraform_EBS_Volume1".

We need a Terraform template that creates a modular Amazon Route 53 DNS infrastructure supporting hosted zones, records, reusable delegation sets, health checks, query logging, VPC associations, cross-account association authorizations, and DNSSEC key-signing keys. Global prefix variables for name ("TEST") and environment ("STAGE") must construct default lowercased resource names when explicit names are omitted, and provisioning across components must be governed by individual boolean flags defaulting to false: enable_route53_zone, enable_route53_record, enable_route53_health_check, enable_route53_delegation_set, enable_route53_zone_association, enable_route53_query_log, enable_route53_vpc_association_authorization, and enable_route53_key_signing_key. Hosted zones default domain name to "domain.localdomain", supporting optional comments, force destroy flags, reusable delegation set IDs, and VPC blocks for private hosted zones. DNS records default type to "A" and allow_overwrite to false, dynamically resolving parent zone IDs or health check IDs from created resources when external IDs are omitted, alongside dynamic routing policy blocks for failover, geolocation, latency, weighted, multivalue answer, and alias configurations. Health checks default type to "HTTP", supporting calculated child threshold rules, CloudWatch alarms, IP endpoints, FQDNs, latency measurements, and string search matching. When enabled, key-signing keys upper-case status values and link to created hosted zones or explicit zone IDs alongside required KMS key ARNs, query logs bind CloudWatch log group ARNs to hosted zones, and zone associations handle VPC IDs across specified regions.

We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive set of IAM roles and custom policies to support containerized application deployments on Amazon ECS with automated scaling and CodeDeploy blue/green deployments.
