We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained chaos engineering environment on AWS Fault Injection Simulator, targeting a small EC2 Auto Scaling Group running behind a minimal VPC with a single public subnet. The template must provision the VPC, subnet, internet gateway, and routing, an Auto Scaling Group of EC2 instances running the latest Amazon ECS-optimized AMI, with SSH access restricted to an admin CIDR block and an accepted SSH public key, and a set of FIS experiment templates that inject failures against these resources: an API-level internal-error fault against EC2's DescribeImages API, an EBS volume I/O pause, EC2 CPU stress, EC2 instance termination, and network connectivity disruption on the subnet, all targeting resources by tag and none configured to auto-stop. Include an S3 bucket for FIS experiment logs with a bucket policy allowing AWS log delivery, the IAM role that FIS assumes to run these experiments with the necessary fault-injection permissions, and the EC2 instance role and profile needed for the instances themselves to run under ECS and SSM.

We need a Terraform template that creates a highly modular AWS VPC infrastructure module supporting IPAM integration, customizable public and private subnets, DHCP options, NAT gateways, flow logs, and default resource governance. The primary VPC creation must be controlled by a create_vpc boolean variable defaulting to true, accepting an IPv4 CIDR block defaulting to "10.0.0.0/16" (or utilizing an IPAM pool via ipv4_ipam_pool_id and ipv4_netmask_length), supporting secondary IPv4 CIDR block associations, and enabling DNS hostnames and DNS support by default. Public and private subnet tiers must be defined via flexible map structures accepting explicit CIDR blocks, availability zone assignments, and IPv6 parameters, alongside dedicated route table definitions that map public subnet traffic through a conditionally created Internet Gateway (create_igw defaulting to true) or private subnet traffic through mapped NAT Gateways deployed with Elastic IPs. The module must support optional egress-only internet gateways for IPv6, customizable network ACLs (with private subnets supporting dedicated ACLs with default allow-all inbound and outbound rules), conditionally created DHCP option sets and associations, and VPC flow logs configured across log destinations with custom formatting and aggregation intervals. Finally, the template must allow adopting and managing default VPC components—specifically the default security group (manage_default_security_group defaulting to false), default network ACL (manage_default_network_acl defaulting to false with default allow rules for IPv4/IPv6), and default route table (manage_default_route_table defaulting to false)—to enforce security compliance across the network boundary.

We need a Terraform template that creates a versatile AWS Transfer Family SFTP server solution supporting public or VPC-hosted endpoints, automated user provisioning, and optional Route 53 DNS mapping. The server identifier must derive from an explicit name variable or fallback to a two-word hyphenated random pet name, defaulting logging to a dynamically provisioned IAM role attached to "AWSTransferLoggingAccess" unless an explicit logging role ARN is provided. If configured for API Gateway authentication, the module must provision an API Gateway authorization IAM role with CloudWatch logging permissions. The server endpoint type must support "PUBLIC", "VPC", or "VPC_ENDPOINT" modes, defaulting to "PUBLIC" with "S3" storage and "SFTP" protocols, while supporting optional FTPS ACM certificates, custom login banners, custom security policies (defaulting to "TransferSecurityPolicy-2023-05"), host keys, structured CloudWatch log destinations, and protocol details for AS2, passive IP, set-stat options, or TLS session resumption. When hosted inside a VPC without pre-existing network resources supplied in endpoint details, it must automatically create a dedicated security group opening port 22 to 0.0.0.0/0 along with an Elastic IP per specified subnet. Furthermore, if a Route 53 hosted zone is specified, create a CNAME record mapping a sub-domain (defaulting to "sftp") to the Transfer Server endpoint. Finally, for each user in a map of SFTP users, provision an IAM role and policy granting list and object access to their specified S3 home directory bucket path, an AWS Transfer user, and associate any matching SSH public keys provided in a secondary user key map.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained Amazon EKS cluster architecture inside a dedicated 192.168.0.0/16 VPC with up to 3 public and 3 private subnets across available availability zones, complete with an Internet Gateway, Elastic IP, NAT Gateway in the first public subnet, public and private route tables, a private DB subnet group, and cluster security groups for control plane and node communication. The cluster name should default to "md-k8s" using variable MD_CLUSTER_NAME, with IAM service roles and custom policy documents providing EKS control plane permissions, ELB management, and CloudWatch metric writing. The template must support optional persistent EC2 node group deployment via variable PERSISTENT_DEPLOYMENT (defaulting to false), which when enabled provisions an SSH node group remote access security group allowing inbound port 22 from private CIDR ranges, an RSA TLS key pair and AWS key pair, a worker node IAM role with attached policies for EKS Worker Nodes, ECR Read Only, SSM Managed Instance Core, CNI, and a detailed AWS Load Balancer Controller policy, a GP3 launch template with 80GB storage, and a managed node group running two c5.2xlarge instances. Additionally, it must support optional Fargate node deployment via variable DEPLOY_FARGATE_NODES (defaulting to false), which provisions a Fargate pod execution role and a Fargate profile targeting default or kube-system namespaces, and if Fargate is deployed without persistent nodes, generates a local kubeconfig file and executes a local-exec provisioner using an OS check data source to patch the CoreDNS deployment compute type annotation.

We need a Terraform template that creates an AWS Transfer Family server infrastructure supporting secure file transfers backed by S3 or EFS storage. The module must generate a fallback two-word pet name with a hyphen separator if an explicit server name is not supplied, defaulting the server type to PUBLIC (with options for VPC or VPC_ENDPOINT) and the storage domain to S3. When logging_role is unspecified, the template must automatically create a dedicated Transfer Family IAM logging role attached to the AWSTransferLoggingAccess policy, and if identity_provider_type is set to API_GATEWAY, it must create an API Gateway auth role permitting CloudWatch log creation. For VPC deployment endpoints, if custom security group IDs or address allocation IDs are omitted from endpoint details, the template must automatically provision a dedicated security group with inbound port 22 access from 0.0.0.0/0 and full egress, alongside an Elastic IP for each specified subnet ID. The architecture must provision a map of SFTP users (mapping usernames to target S3 bucket paths) where each user receives an automatically generated IAM role and policy scoped exclusively to listing and managing objects within their specific folder path, alongside SSH public key associations when provided. Additionally, if hosted_zone is specified, the template must look up the Route 53 zone and create a CNAME record using a customizable subdomain prefix (defaulting to "sftp") pointing to the Transfer Family server endpoint, while defaulting force_destroy to true and applying the "TransferSecurityPolicy-2023-05" security policy.

We need a Terraform template that creates a feature-rich, highly configurable Amazon S3 storage module using the CloudDrove labeling module (clouddrove/labels/aws version 0.15.0) to generate standard resource names and tags based on name, environment, repository, attributes, and managedby variables. S3 bucket creation must be governed by a boolean flag create_bucket (defaulting to true) and support force_destroy, bucket_prefix, and object lock enabling. The template must conditionally support attaching an IAM bucket policy document when bucket_policy is enabled, configuring transfer acceleration to "Enabled" when acceleration_status is true, setting request payer to "Requester" when request_payer is true, enabling bucket versioning when versioning is true, configuring access logging targeting target_bucket and target_prefix when logging is true, and configuring server-side encryption defaulting to AES256 or "aws:kms" with a KMS master key ID when enable_server_side_encryption and enable_kms are toggled. Additional conditional features must include object lock default retention rules (supporting governance/compliance modes, days, or years), CORS rules, static website hosting with index/error documents and redirect routing rules from "docs/" to "documents/", canned ACLs or custom access control policy grants using an owner canonical user ID, and comprehensive object lifecycle rules that depend on versioning being established first to handle multipart upload aborts, current object expirations, noncurrent object expirations, and transitions to Standard-IA, Glacier, or Deep Archive storage classes.

We need a Terraform template that creates a multi-tier, dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 AWS network architecture to host a secure three-tier application environment. The stack must deploy a VPC tagged "main-vpc" with a default IPv4 CIDR block of "10.16.0.0/16", Amazon-provided IPv6 CIDR assignment enabled (controlled by is_ipv6_enabled defaulting to true), default instance tenancy, and both DNS hostnames and DNS support enabled by default. To calculate subnet allocations, the template must use the "hashicorp/subnets/cidr" module (version 1.0.0) to dynamically calculate IPv4 subnets using 4 additional bits (/20 subnets) and IPv6 subnets using 8 additional bits (/64 subnets) across a list of subnet objects (sn_details) containing subnet names, target availability zones, and public/private indicators, defaulting to 12 subnets across three availability zones for web (public), app (private), database (private), and reserved (private) tiers. An Internet Gateway tagged with a name prefixed by "main-igw-vpc-" followed by the VPC's resource ID must be attached to the VPC, and a public route table tagged "public-rt-web" routing all IPv4 ("0.0.0.0/0") and IPv6 ("::/0") traffic to the Internet Gateway must be created and associated exclusively with all subnets marked as public. Finally, security groups must be provisioned for each tier: a "web_sg" permitting ingress port 443 (TLS) and port 22 (SSH) from "0.0.0.0/0" and egress port 443 to "app_sg"; an "app_sg" permitting ingress port 443 from "web_sg" and egress port 443 to "db_sg"; and a "db_sg" permitting ingress port 443 from "app_sg".

We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive, modular AWS WAF Classic security stack to inspect and protect web applications against unauthorized traffic and web exploit vectors. The template must feature explicit boolean enable toggles for each WAF component, including IP sets, standard rules, rule groups, Web ACLs, rate-based rules, byte match sets, geo match sets, regex match sets, regex pattern sets, size constraint sets, SQL injection match sets, and XSS match sets. All resource names should automatically default to a lowercase combination of a service name variable defaulting to "TEST" and an environment variable defaulting to "STAGE" unless custom names are explicitly provided. Rate-based rules must support setting an upper-case rate key (defaulting to "IP") and a rate limit (defaulting to 100), while standard rules and rate-based rules dynamically link to created IP sets as default predicate targets when data IDs are omitted. Additionally, regex match sets should default to referencing created regex pattern sets, rule groups should link to created WAF rules, and Web ACLs must support dynamic configuration of default actions, rule associations with override actions, and logging configurations with redacted fields.

We need a Terraform template that creates an automated CloudWatch Synthetics canary monitoring infrastructure to execute continuous health checks within a VPC and trigger notifications upon failure. The template must provision an execution IAM role with a randomized two-word pet name prefix for Lambda execution, granting full S3 permissions, CloudWatch metric writing, CloudWatch logging, and EC2 ENI network interface management. An S3 bucket defaulting to "benchmark-canary-bucket-tf5x" with force destroy enabled, configurable versioning (defaulting to false), public access blocks, default CORS rules, and KMS server-side encryption must store canary artifacts. KMS key management should utilize an enable toggle (defaulting to true) for a custom KMS key with alias "alias/benchmark-canary-key", a 10-day deletion window, key rotation enabled, and a policy granting key access to CloudWatch and account root. An SNS topic named "benchmark-canary-topic" encrypted with the KMS key must publish failure notifications to an email subscription defaulting to "nobody@example.com", supported by an SNS topic policy allowing CloudWatch alarms to publish. The module must iterate over a map of VPC canary configurations to deploy aws_synthetics_canary resources inside specified subnet and security group lists, accepting either inline zip files or S3 artifact sources, with a 120-second execution timeout and configurable schedule expressions. Finally, each canary must include a CloudWatch metric failure alarm triggering on 1 or more failures in a 60-second period that sends alerts to the SNS topic, alongside an optional success percent metric alarm controlled by a boolean flag (defaulting to false) that sends OK notifications to the SNS topic when success falls below 90 percent.

We need a Terraform template that creates a highly customizable VPC module supporting multi-tier subnet architecture and configurable NAT gateway routing. The template must feature a main creation toggle defaulting to true, a configurable VPC CIDR block defaulting to "10.0.0.0/16", and options to enable DNS hostnames and DNS support (both defaulting to true). Subnet tiers must support lists of CIDR blocks for public, private, and isolated intra subnets mapped across a provided list of availability zone names or IDs, automatically generating subnet Name tags using configurable tier suffixes ("public", "private", "intra") and availability zone identifiers unless explicit name lists are supplied. When public subnets are present, the module should support map public IP on launch toggles (defaulting to false) and conditionally provision an Internet Gateway based on a creation toggle (defaulting to true) attached to a dedicated public route table with a default 0.0.0.0/0 route. Additionally, when private subnets, public subnets, and NAT gateways are enabled via the NAT gateway toggle (defaulting to false), the module must create Elastic IPs and NAT Gateways up to the minimum count of public or private subnets, establishing individual private route tables with 0.0.0.0/0 NAT routes associated with each private subnet, while intra subnets maintain isolated route tables without external internet routes.

We need a Terraform template that creates a unified, dual-mode API Gateway module capable of provisioning either an HTTP API (v2) or a REST API (v1) with optional VPC links, custom domain mappings, API keys, and custom Lambda authorizers. The API type must be determined by a variable defaulting to "http", using a default API name of "benchmark-api", and deploying stages named using the environment name value followed by the suffix "-stage". For HTTP APIs, the template should support dynamic route mappings, auto-deployed stages, custom domain configurations with TLS 1.2 regional ACM certificates, optional Route 53 alias A records, and HTTP VPC links created across private subnets. For REST APIs, the module must support dynamic resource path mapping, route methods with path parameter overrides, optional IP source restriction resource policies, automatic redeployment triggers, usage plans with API keys saved as SecureString parameters in SSM Parameter Store, and custom Lambda authorizers featuring Node.js 16.x functions, invocation roles, and execution policies. Additionally, when a VPC link is enabled for REST APIs, the setup must automatically provision an internal Network Load Balancer across private subnets, a target group targeting an ALB ID at a configurable TCP port (defaulting to 443) with HTTPS health checks, a target group attachment, a TCP listener, and an API Gateway VPC link targeting the load balancer ARN.

We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive, secure AWS CloudTrail logging architecture for auditing and compliance across account activities. The setup must provision a dedicated CloudTrail trail, an S3 log storage bucket, a CloudWatch Log Group, an IAM role for CloudWatch Logs ingestion, a KMS key for encryption, and an optional SNS notification topic. The S3 bucket name must default to dynamic generation incorporating account ID, region, and a random 8-character lowercase suffix if unspecified, featuring configurable force destroy (defaulting to true), versioning configuration (defaulting to false), and an S3 bucket policy permitting CloudTrail ACL checks and put-object actions with full control. CloudTrail log file encryption must use a dedicated KMS key with a 30-day deletion window, automated annual key rotation, an alias prefix, and a key policy granting permissions to root IAM users, CloudTrail encryption contexts, CloudWatch Logs, and an optional role ARN provided for log decryption. The CloudWatch Log Group must default to retaining logs for 90 days, populated by a dedicated IAM role and policy allowing CloudTrail to create log streams and put log events. CloudTrail itself must enforce log file validation, include global service events (defaulting to true), multi-region trails (defaulting to true), logging toggles (defaulting to true), organization trail toggles (defaulting to false), event selectors with configurable read/write types (defaulting to "All"), management events (defaulting to true), dynamic data resource selectors, and dynamic insight selectors. Finally, the module should support conditionally creating an SNS topic for alerts with a topic policy allowing CloudTrail publishing, falling back to an existing SNS topic ARN if topic creation is disabled.

We need a Terraform template that creates a secure static website hosting architecture on AWS using Amazon S3, CloudFront, ACM, and Route 53. The infrastructure must provision a private S3 bucket whose name defaults to a custom name variable, falling back to an optional domain name variable, or an automated fallback name prefixed with "webapp-template-" appended with an 8-byte hexadecimal random ID if both are blank, with optional bucket versioning defaulting to false. CloudFront access to the bucket must be enforced using Origin Access Control with an S3 bucket policy allowing s3:GetObject strictly when the source ARN matches the CloudFront distribution ARN. The CloudFront distribution must default to PriceClass_100, IPv6 enabled, index.html as the default root object, HTTPS redirection across all behaviors, and an origin signing protocol of SigV4. It must utilize the AWS-managed Managed-CachingOptimized cache policy by default while applying an ordered cache behavior with Managed-CachingDisabled specifically for the /index.html path, alongside default custom error responses mapping HTTP 403 and 404 error codes to a 404 response code with a 10-second minimum TTL returning /index.html. Furthermore, if a domain name is specified, the template must require a non-empty Route 53 hosted zone ID, automatically creating an ACM certificate in us-east-1 with DNS validation, Route 53 DNS validation records, certificate validation, Route 53 alias A records targeting the distribution, SNI-only SSL support with a default minimum TLS version of TLSv1.2_2021, and optional www. domain aliases with wildcard subject alternative names controlled by a boolean flag defaulting to false.

We need a Terraform template that creates a customizable multi-tier AWS VPC network across 3 active availability zones for hosting production and administrative workloads, defaulting to us-east-1. The VPC must use a base CIDR block constructed as "10.20.0.0/16" with DNS hostnames and DNS support enabled, tagged with default global tags ("Author" = "Fairwinds", "Managed By" = "Terraform"), and connected to an Internet Gateway named "vpc". Across 3 active availability zones (parsed from a comma-separated list of availability zone names, defaulting to a preconfigured set of us-east-1 availability zones), create 4 distinct subnet tiers per availability zone using specific subnet CIDR suffixes appended to the base CIDR: admin subnets (suffixes ".0.0/21", ".8.0/21", ".16.0/21"), public subnets (suffixes ".32.0/21", ".40.0/21", ".48.0/21"), private production subnets (suffixes ".64.0/21", ".72.0/21", ".80.0/21"), and private working subnets (suffixes ".96.0/21", ".104.0/21", ".112.0/21"). Routing must feature one shared public route table associated with all public subnets routing "0.0.0.0/0" to the Internet Gateway, and dedicated per-AZ private route tables (named "private_az1", "private_az2", "private_az3") associated with all admin, private production, and private working subnets. Outbound internet connectivity for private subnets must be supplied via per-AZ Elastic IPs and NAT Gateways deployed into each public subnet (governed by multi_az_nat_gateway set to 1 and single_nat_gateway set to 0), and an S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint must be conditionally provisioned when enable_s3_vpc_endpoint is set to true using a full access policy associated with all private route tables.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained, production-style web backend platform on AWS Fargate, deployed into a new VPC spanning two public and two private subnets across two availability zones in the region, with an internet gateway and separate route tables for the public and private subnets. Traffic should reach the application through an internet-facing Application Load Balancer listening on HTTP port 80 and forwarding to a target group with health checks against a configurable health-check path, backed by an ECS Fargate service split roughly 20 percent on-demand Fargate and 80 percent Fargate Spot capacity, running with a deployment circuit breaker and automatic rollback enabled, and target tracking auto-scaling on both average CPU and memory utilization keeping the service between 2 and 4 running tasks. The task should initially run a placeholder public nginx container image exposing a configurable application port (default 80) that will later be replaced by CI/CD, and it should read its PostgreSQL connection string from environment variables pointing at a companion RDS PostgreSQL database (a small single-AZ instance is sufficient) placed in the private subnets, using a default username and password of "postgres" for initial bootstrapping and a database named "mydb". A dedicated container registry repository should be created for the application image with a lifecycle rule that automatically expires untagged images after 14 days. For CI/CD, set up an IAM OpenID Connect identity provider trusting GitHub Actions' token issuer, with an assumable role restricted to workflows from a given GitHub organization or account (accepted as an input parameter) that is permitted to build and push container images, register new ECS task definitions, pass the task's own IAM roles, update the ECS service, and list, describe, and clean up old task definitions. Configure security groups so that only the load balancer can reach the application containers on any port, only the application containers can reach the database on its PostgreSQL port, and outbound internet access is otherwise unrestricted, and give the ECS execution and task roles the standard managed ECS task execution permissions needed to pull images and write logs.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained security and identity management foundation for a HashiStack cluster deployment. The module must define input variables for cluster_tag defaulting to "default", enable_key_rotation defaulting to false, and a machine_roles map (mapping role names to sets of policy identifier strings) defaulting to an empty map. Provision a KMS key for Vault unsealing with description "resinstack:vault:seal:{cluster_tag}", annual key rotation set to enable_key_rotation, and a tag "resinstack:cluster" matching cluster_tag. Create seven Secrets Manager secrets tagged with cluster_tag for HashiStack tokens and keys, named "resinstack-{name}-{cluster_tag}" for consul-agent-token, consul-gossip-key, nomad-client-consul-token, nomad-gossip-key, nomad-server-consul-token, nomad-vault-token, and vault-consul-token. Define IAM policies for unsealing Vault via KMS (permitting "kms:Encrypt", "kms:Decrypt", "kms:DescribeKey"), describing EC2 instances ("ResinStackReadTags", permitting "ec2:DescribeInstances"), and retrieving secret values from Secrets Manager tailored for clients (the consul-agent-token, consul-gossip-key, and nomad-client-consul-token secrets), Nomad servers (consul-agent-token, consul-gossip-key, nomad-gossip-key, nomad-server-consul-token, and nomad-vault-token), Consul servers (consul-gossip-key), and Vault servers (consul-gossip-key and vault-consul-token). Dynamically iterate over machine_roles to create EC2 assume roles with a 12-hour maximum session duration and corresponding instance profiles named "resinstack-{role name}-{cluster_tag}", attaching the appropriate IAM policies when their identifiers ("read-tags", "vault-kms", "nomad-keys", "consul-keys", "vault-keys", "client-keys") are present in the role's policy set. Output the Vault KMS key ID, a map of secret names from Secrets Manager, and maps of the generated machine role names and instance profile names.

We need a Terraform template that creates a custom multi-AZ networking foundation for a blog web application. The self-contained stack must deploy a VPC configured with a 64.0.0.0/16 CIDR block, default instance tenancy, DNS support, DNS hostnames, and disabled ClassicLink, tagged with an environment prefix defaulting to "elluis_codes_limited_network". Across a provided map of three availability zones (mapped to subnet offset values 11, 22, and 33), the infrastructure must create public subnets with auto-assigned public IP addresses and private subnets, using 8-bit CIDR offsets to calculate distinct subnet ranges. Outbound internet connectivity must be enabled via an Internet Gateway attached to the VPC and public route tables routing all traffic out to the Internet Gateway. To support private network egress, allocate an Elastic IP for every availability zone and deploy a NAT Gateway into each corresponding public subnet, connecting them to dedicated per-AZ private route tables that route 0.0.0.0/0 traffic to the NAT Gateways while ignoring future changes to route table and NAT gateway associations.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained Amazon GuardDuty threat detection and findings export infrastructure. The setup must provision a primary GuardDuty detector enabled by default with configurable data sources for S3 logs, Kubernetes audit logs, and EC2 malware scanning, featuring finding publishing frequencies defaulting to "FIFTEEN_MINUTES" and a local-exec provisioner to set EBS snapshot preservation to "RETENTION_WITH_FINDING" or "NO_RETENTION" based on a snapshot retention toggle (defaulting to false). The template must dynamically support custom finding filters, IP sets, threat intelligence sets, and publishing destinations. When IP sets, threat intel sets, or S3 publishing is enabled, the module must automatically provision supporting encryption keys and S3 buckets, including a multi-region KMS key with automated key rotation and a 7-day deletion window, a primary versioned S3 bucket encrypted with the KMS key and configured with server-side access logging to a dedicated log bucket, an IAM replication role and policy, and a secondary replica bucket in a replica region using cross-region provider settings for 15-minute S3 Replication Time Control.

We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive Amazon GuardDuty threat detection architecture with configurable data sources, findings filters, trusted IP sets, threat intelligence lists, and encrypted S3 export capabilities. The template must deploy a primary GuardDuty detector enabled by default with S3 protection, Kubernetes audit log protection, and EBS volume malware scanning configured, defaulting notification publishing frequencies to fifteen-minute intervals and executing a local provisioner to set EBS snapshot retention settings based on boolean input. When IP sets, threat intel sets, or S3 publishing destination exports are configured, the stack must automatically provision all necessary self-contained supporting infrastructure, including a multi-region KMS customer managed key for primary bucket encryption, a replica KMS key for cross-region disaster recovery replication in an optional target region, IAM replication roles and policies, and three versioned S3 buckets: a primary findings bucket, a dedicated log bucket for target access logging, and a replica bucket configured for cross-region object replication with encrypted transport policies and public access blocks enforced. Additionally, the module must support dynamic creation of GuardDuty filters based on flexible criteria mappings, manage inline S3 objects for custom IP sets and threat intelligence content, and support publishing destinations pointing to the provisioned KMS-encrypted primary bucket.

We need a Terraform template that creates a dedicated IAM user with programmatic access credentials for API integration testing and monitoring. The stack must deploy an IAM user at root path "/" defaulting in name to "postman-user" along with a set of IAM access keys, attaching policies that grant global read-only access for API Gateway ("apigateway:GET") and CloudWatch metrics ("cloudwatch:GetMetricData", "cloudwatch:ListMetrics"). Additionally, if an optional cognito_user_pool_arn variable (defaulting to an empty string) is supplied, the template must conditionally create and attach an IAM policy granting "cognito-idp:AdminInitiateAuth" permissions specifically scoped to that Cognito user pool ARN.

We need a Terraform template that creates the IAM roles, policies, attachments, and instance profiles required to support an Amazon EKS control plane and worker node group with Cluster Autoscaler integration. The template must declare a cluster_name variable defaulting to "legion" and establish two IAM roles: one named with a "tf-" prefix followed by the cluster name value for the master control plane, and another named with the same prefix followed by the cluster name value and a "-node" suffix for the worker nodes. The master role must allow assume role trust for the EKS service and attach the AWS managed policies "AmazonEKSClusterPolicy" and "AmazonEKSServicePolicy". The worker node role must allow assume role trust for EC2, attach the managed policies "AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy", "AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy", and "AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly", and be associated with a matching EC2 instance profile whose name follows the same "tf-" prefix, cluster name value, and "-node" suffix pattern. Additionally, the worker node role must be attached to a custom, dynamically-generated IAM policy whose name is prefixed with "eks-worker-autoscaling-" followed by the cluster name value, permitting global describe actions for Auto Scaling groups, Auto Scaling instances, launch configurations, tags, and launch template versions, while restricting capacity modification actions ("autoscaling:SetDesiredCapacity", "autoscaling:TerminateInstanceInAutoScalingGroup", and "autoscaling:UpdateAutoScalingGroup") strictly to resources tagged with a key of "kubernetes.io/cluster/" followed by the cluster name value, equal to "owned", and "k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/enabled" equal to "true".

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained network infrastructure module in AWS to host web server and database workloads. The stack must deploy a VPC defaulting to CIDR block "172.69.0.0/16" tagged "vpc_name", containing a public subnet defaulting to "172.69.1.0/24" tagged "public_subnet" and a private subnet defaulting to "172.69.2.0/24" tagged "private_subnet". Connect the VPC to an internet gateway tagged "igw_tag" and establish a public route table tagged "rtb_tag" that routes "0.0.0.0/0" traffic to the internet gateway and associates directly with the public subnet. Furthermore, provision a web server security group named "webserver-sg_<vpc_id>" tagged "web-server_security_group" supporting dynamic ingress rules (defaulting to TCP port 80 and port 22 open to "0.0.0.0/0") with full outbound egress, alongside a database security group named "database-sg_<vpc_id>" that permits TCP ingress on port 3306.

We need a Terraform template that creates the IAM roles, policies, and instance profiles necessary to support the AWS Cloud Controller Manager and container registry integration for downstream Kubernetes control plane and worker nodes. The module must define a configurable map of tags defaulting to an empty map and create two IAM roles for EC2 assume role access named "aws_ccm_k8s_controlplane" and "aws_ccm_k8s_worker", each associated with a matching EC2 instance profile of the same name. The control plane role must be attached to an IAM policy named "aws_ccm_k8s_controlplane" granting global permissions for EC2 networking, Auto Scaling group description, Elastic Load Balancing management, KMS key description, and service-linked role creation. The worker role must be attached to an IAM policy named "aws_ccm_k8s_worker" granting permissions to describe EC2 instances and regions, along with read-only access to ECR repositories to fetch container images.

We need a Terraform template that creates a foundational IAM security structure with user groups and MFA-enforced administrative roles for multi-user access management. The template must define a configurable name variable defaulting to "awscademo-" to serve as a resource prefix and include default tags for contact, deployment method, deployment date, and infinite TTL. Provision three distinct IAM groups named with the prefix: a demo users group attached to a custom self-management policy allowing users to change their own passwords, manage access keys, upload SSH public keys, and manage virtual MFA devices (including deactivating their own MFA only when MFA is present); a read-only users group attached to the AWS managed ReadOnlyAccess policy; and an MFA superadmin group. Additionally, create an administrative IAM role named with the prefix and truncated to a 31-character name prefix, permitting account root assume-role access with a maximum session duration of 12 hours (43200 seconds), accompanied by an admin policy that grants full administrator permissions conditioned on MFA presence, and attach a group policy to the MFA superadmin group allowing group members to assume this admin role when MFA is present.

We need a Terraform template that creates self-contained IAM OIDC identity providers and operator IAM roles for Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (ROSA) clusters to enable STS web identity federation. The module must accept a list of cluster objects, each containing a cluster ID and an operator role prefix, and default variables for the OIDC provider URL "https://rh-oidc.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com" and its provider thumbprint "917e732d330f9a12404f73d8bea36948b929dffc". For each cluster in the list, create an IAM OpenID Connect Provider configured with client IDs "openshift" and "sts.amazonaws.com" tagged with the cluster ID, alongside six dedicated operator IAM roles that trust web identity assume-role requests from the cluster's federated OIDC provider for specific service accounts: the cloud credential operator role ("{operator_role_prefix}-openshift-cloud-credential-operator-cloud-c" for "system:serviceaccount:openshift-cloud-credential-operator:cloud-credential-operator"), the cloud network config role ("{operator_role_prefix}-openshift-cloud-network-config-controller-c" for "system:serviceaccount:openshift-cloud-network-config-controller:cloud-network-config-controller"), the EBS CSI drivers role ("{operator_role_prefix}-openshift-cluster-csi-drivers-ebs-cloud-cre" for service accounts "aws-ebs-csi-driver-operator" and "aws-ebs-csi-driver-controller-sa"), the image registry role ("{operator_role_prefix}-openshift-image-registry-installer-cloud-cr" for service accounts "cluster-image-registry-operator" and "registry"), the ingress operator role ("{operator_role_prefix}-openshift-ingress-operator-cloud-credential" for "system:serviceaccount:openshift-ingress-operator:ingress-operator"), and the machine API role ("{operator_role_prefix}-openshift-machine-api-aws-cloud-credentials" for "system:serviceaccount:openshift-machine-api:machine-api-controllers"). Each role must include tags indicating the cluster ID, role prefix "ManagedOpenShift", operator namespace, and operator name, and attach its corresponding pre-existing account IAM policy using the naming convention "arn:aws:iam::{account_id}:policy/ManagedOpenShift-...".

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained IAM access management infrastructure to support administrative, CI/CD, and serverless deployment workloads. The stack must establish four IAM groups with distinct paths and inline policies: an "admin" group with path "/admin/" granting full wildcard administrative permissions, an "admin-terraform-cloud" group with path "/admin_terraform_cloud/" also granted full wildcard administrative permissions, a "github" group with path "/github/" assigned an inline policy permitting targeted ACM, CloudFront, IAM, Lambda, Route53, S3, and SQS actions, and a "serverless" group with path "/serverless/" assigned a dedicated policy covering ACM, CloudFront, IAM, Lambda, CloudWatch Logs, Route53, S3, and SQS actions. Additionally, the template must provision corresponding IAM users and memberships—specifically "admin" in the admin group, "admin-macbook-pro" in the admin group with an access key, "admin-terraform-cloud" in the admin-terraform-cloud group with an access key, "github" in the github group, and "serverless" in the serverless group. To complete the serverless tooling access, create an IAM role named "serverless" with path "/serverless/" that allows trust assumptions for Lambda and Edge Lambda services, attaching a customer managed policy named "serverless" with path "/serverless/" containing the identical serverless policy permissions.

We need a Terraform template that creates a secure IAM access management framework to enforce multi-factor authentication for user self-management and administrative role assumption. The setup must utilize standardized CloudPosse label modules for consistent naming using namespace, environment, name, tags, and attributes variables across both an admin group and a non-admin group. A self-management policy must be attached to both groups allowing members to manage their own passwords, access keys, virtual MFA devices, and list account MFA devices and password policies, while requiring active MFA specifically to deactivate their virtual MFA devices. The admin group must additionally receive a policy granting permission to assume a dedicated admin role, strictly requiring MFA present for both role assumption and the role's trust policy targeting the account root principal. The admin role must be attached to the AWS-managed AdministratorAccess policy, and both groups must conditionally manage user memberships based on provided lists of admin and non-admin user names.

We need a Terraform template that creates a secure IAM access management framework defining dedicated user groups and role-based administrative privileges with MFA enforcement. The configuration must establish an admin IAM group and an associated IAM role with full AWS AdministratorAccess permissions, alongside policy documents that allow admin users to manage their own user credentials and MFA devices while requiring MFA presence to assume the admin role. Additionally, it must configure a secondary non-admin IAM group with self-management IAM permissions for generic users, using CloudPosse null label modules for standardized resource naming across environments. We need a Terraform template that creates a reusable AWS Organizations governance module for our management account, letting us optionally attach a set of Service Control Policies to organizational units or the organization root supplied as input parameters. The module should support independently toggled SCPs that: deny all root-user actions, restrict API calls to a caller-supplied list of allowed AWS regions, block disabling of core security services such as CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Config, Security Hub, Access Analyzer, Macie, Inspector, and Detective along with the S3 account-level public access block, enforce encryption on new RDS instances and EBS volumes and require at least a 14-day KMS key deletion window, block making AMIs or EBS snapshots public, prevent member accounts from leaving the organization, protect VPC flow logs from deletion, block deactivating MFA devices or creating root access keys, and require IMDSv2 on all new and modified EC2 instances. We need a Terraform template that creates a complete multi-AZ networking stack for AWS, defaulting to us-east-1, to securely host public web applications and private backend services. The VPC must use a default CIDR block of "10.0.0.0/16" with DNS hostnames and DNS support enabled, tagged with a default vpc_name of "benchmark-vpc" alongside a configurable map of additional tags. Subnets must be dynamically calculated using cidrsubnet functions across all available opt-in availability zones, splitting the CIDR range evenly into matching public subnets (mapping public IPs on launch) and private subnets. Outbound connectivity requires an Internet Gateway, a dedicated Elastic IP, and a NAT Gateway positioned in the first public subnet. Public security group rules must allow HTTP and HTTPS inbound from everywhere, SSH inbound restricted to the CIDR ranges specified in the ssh_inbound list variable (defaulting to ["10.0.0.0/16"]), and HTTP/HTTPS outbound everywhere. Public NACL rules must allow ingress for HTTP, HTTPS, ephemeral ports (1024-65535), and SSH (using rule numbers starting at 100 for each allowed SSH CIDR), while permitting egress for HTTP, HTTPS, and ephemeral ports. Private NACL rules must allow ingress for HTTP and HTTPS from the public subnets' CIDRs alongside ephemeral ports from everywhere, while permitting egress for HTTPS to everywhere, local ephemeral return traffic to the private subnets, and ephemeral traffic to the public subnets.

We need a Terraform template that creates a multi-tier AWS VPC network infrastructure designed for agentless security scanning workloads across up to 3 available availability zones in the region. The setup must feature a VPC with DNS hostnames and DNS support enabled defaulting to CIDR "10.0.0.0/16" and name tag "DatatogAgentlessScanner", applying default tags for Datadog integration ("Datadog" = "true", "DatadogAgentlessScanner" = "true"). The module must dynamically compute public and offset private subnets across the availability zones, an Internet Gateway with a public route table routing 0.0.0.0/0 to the gateway, a single Elastic IP and NAT Gateway placed in the first public subnet, and a private route table routing 0.0.0.0/0 to the NAT Gateway. Additionally, it must establish private network connectivity via an S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint associated with both route tables, an interface VPC endpoint security group permitting inbound TCP port 443 from the VPC CIDR block, interface VPC endpoints for Lambda and EBS deployed across private subnets with private DNS enabled, and optional SSM interface VPC endpoints for "ec2messages", "ssmmessages", and "ssm" controlled by a boolean flag defaulting to false.

We need a Terraform template that creates a versatile AWS security group management module to manage network access controls for application workloads. Resource naming and tagging must integrate with the git-based label module git::https://github.com/sohanyadav/terraform-aws-labels.git?ref=v1.0.0, appending -sg for new security groups and -prefix-list for managed prefix lists. Both new and existing security group rule management must support separate categorized rule inputs for ingress and egress based on CIDR blocks, self-referencing rules, source security group IDs, and prefix lists (defaulting to the newly created prefix list when unspecified).

We need a Terraform template that creates a dedicated third-party IAM integration role to enable read-only cost optimization and waste-monitoring analysis via CloudForecast. The IAM role must configure an assume-role trust policy permitting cross-account access from the external principal "arn:aws:iam::656227328603:root" conditioned strictly on matching a customizable external ID variable defaulting to "benchmark-external-id", with the role name controlled by a variable defaulting to "CloudForecast-ZeroWaste". We need a Terraform template that creates a set of specialized IAM service users and policies to manage cost reporting, database disaster recovery, data exports, and automated machine image building for a cloud deployment platform. We need a Terraform template that creates a custom VPC network module for hosting a Datadog agentless scanner infrastructure with configurable SSM support. The setup should deploy a VPC with configurable CIDR block defaulting to 10.0.0.0/16, enabling both DNS support and DNS hostnames, and assign default tags alongside mandatory Datadog scanning tags. Dynamically split subnets across up to 3 available availability zones in the target region, assigning public and private subnets derived from 10.0.0.0/16 with netmask offsets, where public subnets route out via an Internet Gateway and private subnets route outbound web traffic through a single NAT Gateway provisioned in the first public subnet. Include full VPC endpoint support for private connectivity, including an S3 Gateway endpoint associated with all route tables, as well as private DNS-enabled Interface endpoints for Lambda and EBS placed inside the private subnets and secured by a dedicated HTTPS endpoint security group allowing port 443 traffic from the VPC CIDR. We need a Terraform template that creates a highly available, self-contained Amazon ECS infrastructure and three-AZ network stack to host containerized PaaS applications. The module must default the AWS region to us-east-1, accept a cluster_name variable defaulting to "benchmark", a vpc_cidr_network_octets string defaulting to "10.0", and a default_tags map defaulting to an empty map. Provision an ECS cluster named with a "dit-paas-" prefix, followed by the cluster name value, and a "-cluster" suffix, alongside a VPC configured with a CIDR block formed from the vpc_cidr_network_octets value followed by ".0.0/16", and DNS hostnames disabled. We need a Terraform template that creates a secure, self-contained VPC network module using CloudPosse community modules to host containerized services with private endpoint access. The network stack must deploy a VPC named via a vpc_name variable defaulting to "benchmark-vpc" with primary IPv4 CIDR defaulting to "172.16.0.0/16", enabling DNS hostnames, disabling generated IPv6 CIDRs, and setting default security group rules to deny all traffic. Access to these interface endpoints must be controlled by a dedicated security group named "vpc_endpoint_sg" that enforces self-referencing TCP ingress and egress rules exclusively on port 443.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained, secure S3 storage and KMS encryption module to store CloudTrail logs for central account and cross-account log delivery. The module must default the AWS region to us-east-1 and establish a primary S3 bucket whose name defaults to "{account_id}-{region}-cloudtrail" unless overridden, alongside a KMS key tagged "cloudtrail-key" with key rotation enabled, a 7-day deletion window, and an alias named "alias/cloudtrail_key". Configure default server-side encryption for the primary bucket using the KMS key, block all public access on both the primary bucket and its access logging bucket, and optionally enable versioning (defaulting to true) and configurable lifecycle rules (defaulting to non-current version expiration after 90 days, STANDARD_IA transition after 30 days, and object expiration after 2557 days). If an external logging bucket name is not provided, automatically create a secondary access logs bucket named "{bucket_name}-access-logs" with "BucketOwnerPreferred" ownership controls and public access blocked, configuring access logging on the primary bucket with a prefix of "{account_id}-{region}-cloudtrail/". Furthermore, restrict the S3 bucket policy to allow CloudTrail service bucket ACL checks and PutObject actions enforcing "bucket-owner-full-control" for the current account ID merged with any account IDs listed in an allowed_account_ids variable list, and construct a KMS key policy allowing root management, CloudTrail data key generation conditioned on CloudTrail ARNs for all permitted account IDs, CloudTrail describe permissions, CloudWatch logs encryption and decryption, and conditional decrypt permissions for any IAM role names specified in a roles_allowed_kms_decrypt variable list.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained VPC module with VPC Flow Logs and flexible VPC endpoint support to securely isolate cloud services. The stack must deploy a VPC with configurable name defaulting to "benchmark-vpc", primary CIDR defaulting to "10.0.0.0/16", instance tenancy defaulting to "default", and DNS hostnames enabled by default in region "us-east-1". Enable VPC Flow Logs for ALL traffic, storing logs in a dedicated CloudWatch Log Group named "/aws/vpc-flow-logs/{var.vpc_name}" with a 180-day retention period, supported by a self-contained IAM role named "vpc_flow_logs_{var.vpc_name}" and policy granting log stream creation and event delivery. Manage the default VPC security group while provisioning two custom security groups: one named "vpc-endpoints-{var.vpc_name}" for standard AWS interface endpoints allowing HTTPS port 443 ingress from and egress to specified source security group IDs, and another for custom endpoint services allowing ingress and egress rules mapped specifically to each custom service port and source security group ID combination. Support dynamically created VPC endpoints including Gateway endpoints for "dynamodb" and "s3" attached to provided route tables, private DNS-enabled Interface endpoints for standard AWS services specified in a set defaulting to ["logs"], and non-private DNS Interface endpoints for custom endpoint services defined by key, service name, and port. Finally, if the "ssm" service is included in the requested AWS endpoint services set, automatically provision an IAM role and instance profile both named "ssm_{var.vpc_name}" with EC2 trust and the "AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore" managed policy attached.

We need a Terraform template that creates a baseline security and encryption-at-rest module establishing account-wide data protection controls. The stack must deploy default EBS encryption enabled at the account level and three separate KMS customer-managed keys with aliases each prefixed "alias/" followed by the project name value and a layer-specific suffix of "-compute", "-observability", or "-storage" for the compute, observability, and storage layers respectively, each with key rotation enabled using a configurable rotation period in days defaulting to 90, a 30-day deletion window, and prevent_destroy lifecycle protection. Configure the compute KMS key policy to permit IAM root access, EC2 service operations for the current account, and Auto Scaling service role usage including grant creation; set the account-level default EBS KMS key to either an optional external key ARN variable or the internal compute KMS key ARN when left blank; configure the observability KMS key policy for IAM root access, CloudWatch Logs conditioned on log group context, CloudTrail, CloudWatch Alarms, SNS, SQS, and EventBridge; and configure the storage KMS key policy for IAM root access, S3 service usage, AWS Config encrypted snapshot delivery, and CloudTrail log encryption. Additionally, enforce account-level public access restrictions by setting EC2 image block public access to "block-new-sharing", EBS snapshot block public access to "block-all-sharing", conditional account-level EC2 instance metadata defaults enforcing required HTTP tokens (IMDSv2) with a configurable hop limit defaulting to 1 when a default-true toggle is set, conditional disabling of EC2 Serial Console access when a default-true toggle is set, and conditional EMR block public access configuration restricting public security groups when a default-true toggle is set.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained, customizable VPC network infrastructure and EC2 inventory node cluster for deployment testing. The module must feature a configurable cluster prefix defaulting to "bench" (restricted to 5-8 characters), a default VPC CIDR of "172.16.0.0/16" with DNS support and DNS hostnames enabled, an Internet Gateway, and a deployment SSH key pair defaulting to "benchmark-keypair" with a valid public key string. The network architecture must dynamically calculate CIDR allocations for user-defined public and private subnet objects across specified availability zones, configuring a default public route table pointing 0.0.0.0/0 to the Internet Gateway and provisioning per-subnet Elastic IPs and public NAT Gateways associated with private route tables for private subnets. Security group rules must establish a default security group supporting full self-referencing intra-group ingress, outbound traffic to 0.0.0.0/0, and custom dynamic ingress CIDR rules. For compute nodes defined via an inventory node list, the setup must retrieve recent AMIs, provision EBS-optimized EC2 instances attached to subnets via index positioning with configurable root volumes and optional Elastic IPs, and construct attached secondary EBS volumes mapped to specified device names and mount points.

We need a Terraform template that creates a versatile VPC networking module named "benchmark-vpc" defaulting to the us-east-1 region with a CIDR block of "10.0.0.0/16", an Internet Gateway, a default security group allowing self-referencing ingress and outbound traffic to 0.0.0.0/0, an additional security group allowing inbound TLS traffic on port 443, and flexible public or private subnet layouts using specific default subnet CIDR allocations ("10.0.1.0/24", "10.0.2.0/24", "10.0.3.0/24", and "10.0.4.0/24"). When private subnets are enabled via a boolean toggle defaulting to true, the template must provision two public subnets in the first two availability zones and two private subnets in those same availability zones using the third and fourth CIDR blocks, while toggling private subnets to false must instead create four public subnets across four availability zones. Furthermore, the private routing infrastructure must support mutually exclusive egress routing strategies controlled by independent boolean toggles: deploying redundant NAT Gateways in each public subnet with associated Elastic IPs and private route tables, deploying redundant NAT EC2 instances (m1.small) using Amazon Linux NAT AMIs in each public subnet with custom security group rules and private route tables pointing to their primary network interfaces, or creating an Egress-Only Internet Gateway with IPv6 egress routes to ::/0.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained AWS infrastructure deployment for benchmarking compute nodes across custom public and private network topologies. The configuration must include an SSH key pair defaulted to benchmark-keypair with an allowed default SSH public key text, where the key pair name must be validated to exceed four characters and the public key text cannot be empty. The network layer must support dynamic lists of public and private subnets where subnet CIDRs can be calculated dynamically using cidrsubnets with a default range offset of 4 when not specified; public subnets must map public IPs on launch and route out via a central Internet Gateway attached to the default route table, while private subnets must each provision dedicated Elastic IPs and public NAT Gateways associated with custom private route tables. The template must set up a default security group that allows all internal intra-security-group ingress traffic, all standard outbound egress traffic, and configurable dynamic ingress rules accepting specific CIDR lists, protocols, and port ranges. Finally, the stack must dynamically provision a list of inventory EC2 instances mapped to targeted subnets, defaulting to m5.xlarge instances running the latest Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.6 x86_64 AMIs with ec2-user as the instance user and an ebs-optimized 30 GB gp2 root volume; these instances must support optional dedicated Elastic IPs, custom secondary EBS volumes with device and mount-point tag tracking, pre-condition validation ensuring at least one subnet exists before launching, and outputs detailing provisioned node metadata, IP addresses, and attached storage volume configurations.

We need a Terraform template that creates a versatile VPC networking and private interface endpoint module supporting either new VPC provisioning or integration with existing infrastructure. The stack must deploy a VPC named via a name variable defaulting to "benchmark-vpc" with primary CIDR "10.0.0.0/16", enabling DNS hostnames and DNS support by default in us-east-1, unless an existing vpc_id is supplied. Unless overridden by pre-existing subnet ID maps, the module must provision public subnets mapping public IPs on launch, private subnets, and database subnets using a default CIDR map across two default availability zones in the us-east-1 region, alongside an RDS database subnet group named using a lowercased version of the VPC name. Outbound routing must be configured via an Internet Gateway and a single Elastic IP-backed NAT Gateway deployed in the first public subnet targeting the private route table, unless an existing_nat_id is provided. Additionally, the template must establish interface VPC endpoints for a configurable list of AWS services defaulting to "ec2", "ecr.api", "ecr.dkr", "s3", "logs", "sts", "elasticloadbalancing", and "autoscaling" attached to all private subnets, secured either by an existing security_group_id or by a newly created endpoint security group named using the VPC's name value followed by the suffix "-vpc-endpoints", that permits inbound HTTPS port 443 traffic from the VPC CIDR.

We need a Terraform template that creates an isolated testing VPC environment to validate AWS Systems Manager Session Manager connectivity for EC2 instances without internet access. The infrastructure must deploy a VPC with CIDR 10.8.0.0/16, enabling DNS support and DNS hostnames, along with a single private subnet with CIDR 10.8.1.0/24 in the first available availability zone. The private subnet must host private DNS-enabled interface VPC endpoints for ssm, ec2messages, ssmmessages, and CloudWatch logs, each auto-accepted and secured by a common service endpoint security group that allows inbound port 443 TCP traffic from the VPC CIDR with no egress rules. Configure a test EC2 instance of type t3.small using the latest Amazon Linux 2 x86_64 EBS-backed AMI running in the private subnet with source/destination checks disabled and attached to an instance security group that allows egress port 443 TCP traffic restricted to the VPC CIDR with no ingress rules. Provide an IAM instance profile and role with permissions for SSM, SSMMessages, EC2Messages, CloudWatch Logs, KMS data key generation, and S3 object actions, ensuring both the IAM role and instance profile names use prefixes based on an application shortcode variable defaulting to "bmk".

We need a Terraform template that creates a secure, private ECS Fargate deployment to run an NGINX service alongside an SSM-managed jumphost for internal testing in us-east-1. The infrastructure must include a VPC with a /16 CIDR block spanning three Availability Zones, featuring three public and three private subnets, one NAT gateway per Availability Zone, and enabled DNS hostnames. To ensure AWS API traffic does not traverse the public internet, configure a gateway VPC endpoint for S3 attached to the private route tables, along with interface endpoints for ECR Docker, ECR API, CloudWatch Logs, Secrets Manager, SSM, and KMS, all secured by a security group allowing inbound HTTPS traffic from the VPC CIDR. For internal routing, establish a private Cloud Map DNS namespace named "private-fargate-crowdnews.hands-on.cloud.local" within the VPC. The container infrastructure requires an ECR repository with mutable tags and scan-on-push enabled, a CloudWatch log group, an ECS cluster, and a Fargate task definition utilizing 512 CPU units and 1024 memory to run the NGINX image on port 80 in awsvpc mode, passing the service discovery namespace ID as an environment variable. Deploy this as a Fargate service with a desired count of 1 task in the private subnets, assign dedicated execution and task IAM roles with necessary inline policies for ECR pulls, logging, parameter access, and service discovery, secure it with a task security group allowing port 80 ingress from the VPC, and register it to the Cloud Map namespace with multivalue A and SRV records using a 10-second TTL and a custom health check failure threshold of 1. To facilitate testing, launch a t3.micro Amazon Linux 2 EC2 instance in the first public subnet using a custom network interface with a static private IP, attach an IAM instance profile with the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore managed policy, and secure it with a security group allowing all inbound traffic from the VPC. Finally, provide a Terraform output containing the exact curl command required to reach the NGINX service via its private service discovery DNS name.

We need a Terraform template that creates a complete benchmark environment in us-east-1 centered around a t3.micro Amazon Linux 2 EC2 instance and its supporting networking and identity infrastructure. The deployment should provision a foundational VPC with a /16 CIDR block and an internet gateway, housing a public subnet with a /24 CIDR that routes all default outbound traffic to the internet gateway while allowing for the injection of custom route definitions. Inside this subnet, deploy the EC2 instance attached via a dedicated network interface configured to dynamically map a public IP on launch, while retaining the logic to optionally allocate and associate a static Elastic IP if requested. The instance must strictly enforce IMDSv2 and utilize a 20 GB encrypted root volume, with the flexibility to conditionally generate and attach an SSH key pair. For secure management, attach an IAM instance profile and role that trusts both the EC2 and SSM services, applying a dedicated IAM policy that explicitly grants SSM Session Manager permissions for control and data channels, alongside a toggleable option to attach the standard AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore managed policy. All deployed resources, including the compute instance, volumes, network interface, subnet, route table, and elastic IP, must adopt a standardized naming convention and tagging structure derived from project, application, environment, and availability zone prefixes, and the template must output the resulting ARNs and IDs of the EC2 instance, IAM role, instance profile, route table, and subnet.

We need a Terraform template that creates a custom Amazon EKS cluster named "demo-eks" with unmanaged worker nodes deployed via a CloudFormation-managed Auto Scaling Group in the default VPC across three availability zones in us-east-1, ensuring the AWS provider applies a default tag of "kubernetes.io/cluster/demo-eks" set to "owned". First, provision the EKS control plane attached to the default VPC's public subnets, utilizing an IAM role named "eksClusterRole" that includes the standard EKS cluster and VPC resource controller policies. For the worker nodes, generate a 4096-bit RSA TLS private key, save it locally to "~/.ssh/eks-aws.pem", and register it as an AWS key pair named "eks_kp". Create a dedicated node security group allowing all outbound traffic, unrestricted internal communication between nodes, and tightly scoped TCP ingress and egress rules on ports 443 and 1025-65535 to permit two-way communication with the EKS control plane's security group. Provision an IAM role named "eks-demo-node" with managed policies for EKS worker nodes, CNI, ECR read-only, and SSM core management, and attach it to an instance profile. Next, configure an EC2 launch template using a t3.medium instance, a 30 GB gp2 root volume, optional IMDSv2 HTTP tokens with a hop limit of 2, the latest Amazon Linux 2 EKS-optimized AMI retrieved via SSM, and a base64-encoded user-data bootstrap script that connects to the cluster and signals a CloudFormation stack upon completion. After incorporating a 30-second delay to allow the launch template to settle, deploy a CloudFormation stack named "eks-cluster-stack" to provision the Auto Scaling Group across the public subnets with a minimum size of 1, desired capacity of 3, and maximum size of 4, ensuring it incorporates an update policy for rolling updates with a maximum batch size of 1, a minimum of 3 instances in service, and a 5-minute pause time. Finally, output the node instance role ARN, the node security group ID, and the newly created Auto Scaling Group ID returned directly by the CloudFormation stack.

We need a Terraform template that creates a secure, highly durable remote state management architecture for multiple EKS stacks, utilizing an S3 backend in us-east-1 with cross-region replication to us-west-1. The deployment must provision a primary S3 bucket named dynamically with the AWS account ID, enforcing versioning, strict public access blocks, and a bucket policy that explicitly denies non-SSL requests. All objects in the primary bucket must be encrypted server-side by default using a new custom KMS key configured with a 7-day deletion window and automatic key rotation. For disaster recovery, provision a replica S3 bucket in the us-west-1 region with identical versioning, SSL enforcement, and public access blocks, secured by its own dedicated replica KMS key. Configure S3 cross-region replication on the primary bucket to automatically replicate KMS-encrypted objects to the replica bucket, attaching an IAM role with the precise permissions required to read the source objects, decrypt them using the primary KMS key, and encrypt them at the destination using the replica key. To support concurrent operations, iterate through a provided map of stack names and regions to deploy individual pay-per-request DynamoDB tables keyed by "LockID" for each stack's state locking, alongside dedicated IAM policies that grant stack-specific access to their respective DynamoDB table, S3 bucket prefix, and KMS key operations. Finally, the template must automatically generate a local "backend.tf" file for each stack within a relative "eks-stacks" directory to seamlessly integrate these backend configurations into our workflows, ensuring all created resources are tagged with a standardized set of state management labels.

We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive EKS-based application environment supported by external PostgreSQL, Redis, and S3 data services in us-east-1. The foundational network must consist of a custom VPC with a /16 CIDR block spanning two Availability Zones, featuring two public and two private /24 subnets, an internet gateway, and a route table allowing outbound internet access for the public subnets, alongside a unified security group permitting inbound traffic from anywhere on ports 22, 443, 5432, 6379, 6380, and 8201. For the container orchestration layer, deploy a version 1.31 EKS cluster associated with a dedicated IAM role containing cluster and VPC controller policies, and a managed node group of c4.2xlarge instances configured with a minimum of 1, a maximum of 3, and a desired capacity of 2 nodes, placed in the public subnets and attached to a node IAM role granting worker, CNI, ECR read-only, and full S3 access permissions. For the persistent data tier, provision a force-destroyable S3 storage bucket, a 400 GB PostgreSQL 14.24 RDS instance on a db.m5.xlarge node skipping final snapshots, and a single-node Redis 7.1 ElastiCache cluster using a cache.t3.small node type. Both the database and the cache must be placed into custom subnet groups mapped to the first public and first private subnets and secured by the unified security group. Finally, the template must expose outputs for the cluster name, deployment region, database endpoint, database name, administrative username, sensitive password, S3 bucket name, Redis host address, Redis port, and the AWS CLI command required to update the local kubeconfig.
